speaker: Unknown
en: We weren't even monetizing, and people were emailing us begging to pay for the product.
zh: 我们当时甚至还没开始变现，人们却在给我们发邮件，恳求付费购买这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: For today's episode, I'm sitting down with John Nerona, co-founder and chief product officer of Gamma, the AI presentation platform that has over 100 million users.
zh: 在今天的这期节目里，我与 Gamma 的联合创始人兼首席产品官 John Nerona 坐下来聊了聊。Gamma 是一个拥有超过一亿用户的 AI 演示平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: We knew this AI thing was going to be big.
zh: 我们当时就知道 AI 这东西会变得很重大。

speaker: Unknown
en: We put all of our resources into it.
zh: 我们把所有资源都投了进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was kind of our Hail Mary moment as a startup.
zh: 作为一家创业公司，那有点像我们的孤注一掷时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: They bet everything on solving one problem, the blank page.
zh: 他们押注一切去解决一个问题：空白页。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it worked, it worked almost too fast.
zh: 而当它成功时，它成功得几乎太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Servers going down every other week.
zh: 服务器每隔一周就宕机一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Support volume we couldn't keep up with.
zh: 客服量多到我们应付不过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best definition I've heard of product market fit is you stop pushing the rock up the hill and you start chasing the rock down the hill.
zh: 我听过对产品市场契合的最好定义是：你不再把石头往山上推，而是开始追着往山下滚的石头跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before that launch, John says that looking back, that weakness may have been one of the luckiest things that ever happened to the company.
zh: John 说，回想起来，在那次发布之前，那个弱点也许是这家公司有过的最幸运的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of my naivete came from looking at some product and saying, I can make it better.
zh: 我的很多天真来自于看着某些产品然后说，我能把它做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because I think it's better doesn't mean the user think it's better.
zh: 仅仅因为我觉得它更好，不代表用户觉得它更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our conversation, John unpacks why Gamma worked.
zh: 在我们的对话中，John 拆解了 Gamma 为什么能成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bet early on and pretty consistently on building a horizontal product rather than a vertical one.
zh: 我们很早就押注，并且相当一贯地押注，做一个横向产品而不是纵向产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually a source of cost and tension in fundraising.
zh: 这实际上在融资过程中是成本和紧张的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gets into the sudden unplanned sprint into enterprise and why he now believes the very guardrails that made Gamma work in 2023 are the same things holding back what today's smarter AI models can do.
zh: 他谈到了突然、计划之外地冲进企业市场，以及为什么他现在相信，让 Gamma 在 2023 年成功的那道护栏，恰恰是如今阻碍更聪明的 AI 模型发挥的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gamma's early success came when LLMs weren't very good yet.
zh: Gamma 的早期成功出现在 LLM 还不太好的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: All those guardrails we put in place are holding these much more intelligent AIs back.
zh: 我们设下的所有那些护栏，正在拖住这些聪明得多的 AI 的后腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're now in a mode not of even adding functionality but trying to throw things out, loosen the requirements, and let AI do more overall.
zh: 我们现在处于一种模式，甚至不是在增加功能，而是试图把东西扔出去、放宽要求，让 AI 在整体上做更多的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's dive in.
zh: 我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of a way to sort of frame part of the discussion is for Gamma, if you go back to like six months before the company was started all the way through today, how would you define like the distinct phases of product market fit for the company?
zh: 作为这场讨论的一种框架方式：对于 Gamma 来说，如果你回溯到公司成立前六个月一直到今天，你会如何定义这家公司在产品市场契合上的各个不同阶段？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let's start with the none era of product market fit.
zh: 好吧，让我们从产品市场契合的「无」时代开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started the company in 2020.
zh: 我们是在 2020 年创办这家公司的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was obviously peak pandemic.
zh: 这显然是疫情的巅峰期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was this period when we saw all these companies like say Zoom and Loom and Slack really blowing up because people were taking a new approach to work.
zh: 在那个时期，我们看到 Zoom、Loom、Slack 这些公司都在爆发式增长，因为人们在采取一种新的工作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was this incredible why now moment of people realizing we're not all in the same room, we're not using the same tools.
zh: 当时有一个难以置信的「为什么是现在」的时刻：人们意识到我们不在同一个房间里，我们不在使用同样的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was the era in which Gemma was born.
zh: 所以那就是 Gemma 诞生的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: The early hypothesis was not about AI.
zh: 早期的假设并不是关于 AI 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was all about remote work driving this transformation.
zh: 它完全是关于远程工作驱动这场变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so
zh: 所以

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a lot of prototyping, a lot of beta concepts.
zh: 我们做了大量的原型，大量的 beta 概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you start working on the company without a product in mind?
zh: 你们是在还没想好产品的情况下开始做这家公司的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we had a problem in mind, I should say, and we had a target.
zh: 嗯，应该说我们心里有一个问题，而且我们有一个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: The target was always PowerPoint.
zh: 目标一直是 PowerPoint。

speaker: Unknown
en: We knew we wanted to reinvent presentations because, first of all, it had a massive TAM.
zh: 我们知道我们想重新发明演示文稿，因为首先，它有一个巨大的 TAM。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was something I took from my previous experiences.
zh: 这是我从以前的经历中带到这儿的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to work on something that had a huge TAM, if you were successful, with a product that nobody liked.
zh: 我想做一件 TAM 巨大的事情——如果你成功了的话——而且是一个没人喜欢的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so PowerPoint checked those two boxes really well.
zh: 所以 PowerPoint 非常符合这两个条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also felt well-suited to our team's skills.
zh: 它也感觉很适合我们团队的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really about front-end design, creativity, productivity.
zh: 它主要关于前端设计、创造力、生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew there was a great product to be built here.
zh: 我知道这里有一个很棒的产品可以做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like a billion people that use PowerPoint and Google Slides every month, and they're not happy with it.
zh: 每个月大约有十亿人在使用 PowerPoint 和 Google Slides，而他们并不满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was kind of always the driving force.
zh: 所以这一直是驱动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought we had a why now.
zh: 我们认为我们有一个「为什么是现在」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we dove in and we said, all right, let's prototype, let's explore, let's see what we can do here.
zh: 于是我们投入进去说，好，我们来做原型，我们来探索，看看我们能在这里做出什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built a product that did okay, I would say.
zh: 我们做出的一个产品，我会说做得还不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had some traction.
zh: 我们有一些增长势头。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, if we're talking 2020 to 2020,
zh: 但是，你知道，如果我们说的是 2020 到 2020——

speaker: Unknown
en: 22-ish, we had basically no product out, just prototypes.
zh: 22 岁左右，我们基本上没有任何产品推出，只有原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: 22, we launch on Product Hunt.
zh: 22 岁，我们在 Product Hunt 上发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get our first thousands of users.
zh: 我们获得了最初的几千名用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we're in the hundreds of monthly actives.
zh: 月活大概在几百人的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have slightly linear growth, but I would say we're in this era of weak to middling product market fit.
zh: 我们有略微线性的增长，但我会说我们还处于从弱到中等的产品市场契合度时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely not red hot.
zh: 绝对算不上红热。

speaker: Unknown
en: At this point, runway starts dwindling.
zh: 到这个时候，现金跑道开始减少。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're starting to figure out where do we go from here?
zh: 我们开始思考，接下来该往哪里走？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we drive more of this?
zh: 我们如何推动更多的增长？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is when the first green shoots of AI are starting to show up.
zh: 而这正是 AI 的第一抹新绿开始显现的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing stable diffusion as a model out there.
zh: 我们看到 Stable Diffusion 作为一个模型存在于世。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing GPT-3, not even ChatGPT yet.
zh: 我们看到了 GPT-3，甚至还没有 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we realized that Gamma's core problem is this blank page problem.
zh: 而我们意识到 Gamma 的核心问题就是这个空白页问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: People come in wanting to make a presentation or whatever, but they're faced with an empty white screen and told, go start from scratch.
zh: 人们进来想做演示文稿或什么的，但他们面对的是一个空白的白色屏幕，被告知：从零开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But why wasn't that a problem for Google Slides or PowerPoint?
zh: 但为什么这对 Google Slides 或 PowerPoint 来说不是一个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's the ironic thing we realized is that in fact it is, but there was no alternative.
zh: 嗯，这就是我们意识到的具有讽刺意味的地方——事实上它就是问题，只是没有别的替代选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that actually is what drove product market fit for us is, you know, we always tell ourselves we're 10x better than PowerPoint, 10x better than Google Slides.
zh: 而这实际上就是为我们带来产品市场契合度的东西，你知道，我们总告诉自己我们比 PowerPoint 好 10 倍，比 Google Slides 好 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But until we actually solved that blank page problem for people, we weren't really.
zh: 但在我们真正为人们解决那个空白页问题之前，我们其实并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was actually the foundational problem with those products is they start in a blank page and you cobble something together out of templates.
zh: 那实际上才是那些产品根本性的问题——它们从一个空白页开始，然后你用模板东拼西凑出点东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there just was no better way technologically to overcome this before.
zh: 而在此之前，技术上也确实没有更好的办法来克服这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the closest was to give people good templates.
zh: 我认为最接近的办法就是给人们好的模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Canvas strategy.
zh: 这是 Canvas 的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also what Notion's done really well in its own kind of separate domain.
zh: 这也是 Notion 在它自己那个独立领域里做得非常好的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we got to now use this ultra powerful kryptonite tool to solve the problem, which was generative AI.
zh: 但我们现在要用这个超级强大的克敌工具来解决这个问题，那就是生成式 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we plugged that in to solve our onboarding challenges.
zh: 于是我们把它接进来，解决我们的新手引导难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How easy was it to identify that that was the bottleneck?
zh: 识别出那就是瓶颈，有多容易？

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it...
zh: 是不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Blindingly obvious.
zh: 一目了然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once we had already launched a product and had it in market, it was blindingly obvious that our activation rate was low.
zh: 一旦我们已经发布了产品并让它进入市场，我们的激活率很低这一点是一目了然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The conversion rate of someone signing up for our product from a landing page and actually getting to a point of seeing value was like appallingly low.
zh: 一个人从落地页注册我们的产品、到真正到达看到价值的那一步，这个转化率低得惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, we're talking five or 10% or something.
zh: 大概是，我们在说的是 5% 或 10% 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as soon as we went to say, well, what would get this number to be 20, 30, 50%, it was like, well, this blank page was staring us in the face is the obvious problem.
zh: 所以当我们一开始问：怎样才能把这个数字变成 20%、30%、50%？答案就是，这个空白页明晃晃地摆在我们眼前，就是那个显而易见的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at that point, yes, it was obvious.
zh: 所以在那个时候，是的，它是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we designed a whole launch around let's overcome that blank page.
zh: 于是我们围绕「让我们克服那个空白页」设计了一整场发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was kind of our Hail Mary moment as a startup.
zh: 那某种程度上是我们作为一家创业公司的孤注一掷时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were down to maybe a year of runway.
zh: 我们只剩下大概一年的现金跑道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were a team of 12.
zh: 我们是一个 12 人的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we knew this AI thing was going to be big.
zh: 但我们知道这个 AI 的东西会很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody knew how big.
zh: 没人知道会有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we wanted to bet on use AI to overcome the blank page problem.
zh: 而我们想押注用 AI 来克服空白页问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we did a big launch around this.
zh: 于是我们围绕这个做了一场大型发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: We put all of our resources into it.
zh: 我们把所有资源都投了进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: We launched it in March 2023.
zh: 我们在 2023 年 3 月发布了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that did take off.
zh: 而那确实起飞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That really did scratch an itch and got us through our first stage of product market fit.
zh: 那真的挠到了痒处，让我们跨过了产品市场契合度的第一阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best definition I've heard of product market fit is you stop pushing the rock up the hill and you start chasing the rock down the hill.
zh: 我听过的对产品市场契合度最好的定义是：你不再把石头推上山，而是开始追着石头下山。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was absolutely what it felt like, especially those first, I would say that first year of 2023 was just, there was such a gap between the capabilities of our product and our team and the demand of what people wanted out of it.
zh: 那绝对就是当时的感觉，尤其是 2023 年最初那一年——我们的产品和团队的能力，与人们对它的需求之间的差距实在太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were just racing to keep up.
zh: 我们只是在拼命追赶。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're talking servers going down every other week, at one point for even days at a time, a support volume we couldn't keep up with, we weren't even monetizing, and people were emailing us begging to pay for the product.
zh: 我们在说的是每隔一周服务器就宕机一次，有一度甚至一次宕机好几天，支持请求量多到我们应接不暇，我们甚至还没有开始收费，人们却发邮件恳求为这个产品付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of as red hot as it gets with product market fit, and we spent the whole next couple years just trying to keep up with that.
zh: 那基本就是产品市场契合度所能达到的最红热的程度了，而接下来整整几年我们都只是在努力跟上它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we're in an era where I think we've finally caught up with that prosumer product market fit.
zh: 现在我们进入了一个时代，我认为我们终于赶上了那种 prosumer 产品的市场契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're finally able to service the demand and scale it and all of that.
zh: 我们终于能够满足需求并将其规模化等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we've entered this new stage of product market fit challenge, which is in the last year or so B2B demand appeared.
zh: 但现在我们进入了市场契合挑战的新阶段，也就是在过去一年左右，B2B 需求出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Suddenly all these companies were already starting to use our product internally.
zh: 突然之间，所有这些公司都已经开始在内部使用我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, we saw this phenomenon of the AI mandate, where the CEO says top-down, we need more AI.
zh: 而且，我们还看到了这种「AI 强制令」的现象，CEO 自上而下地说，我们需要更多 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's drive this as a priority.
zh: 让我们把它作为优先事项来推动。

speaker: Unknown
en: They survey their employees, and they say, what are the top things you wish you could do with AI?
zh: 他们调查自己的员工，问，你最希望用 AI 做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, everyone needs just a chat tool, for sure.
zh: 嗯，当然，每个人都需要一个聊天工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: The engineers all need a tool like Cursor or Claude Code or whatever.
zh: 所有这类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out the third use case that's bubbling up over and over is presentations.
zh: 而事实证明，第三个不断冒出来的用例是演示文稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are wasting all this time just like formatting their PowerPoints and Google Slides.
zh: 人们浪费了这么多时间，只是在给他们的 PowerPoint 和 Google Slides 做排版。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we hit this new source of product market fit that we were once again woefully unprepared for.
zh: 于是我们碰上了这个新的市场契合来源，而我们再一次完全没有准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had no sales team, no compliance, no anything.
zh: 我们没有销售团队，没有合规，什么都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for the last year in building up that B2B motion, basically from scratch and getting it in place.
zh: 于是在过去一年里，我们基本上是从零开始搭建那套 B2B 运作流程，并把它建立起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before you solve the onboarding problem, was the product for people that got through onboarding insanely high NPS and retentive?
zh: 在你解决引导问题之前，那些通过了引导流程的用户，产品对他们来说是否有着极高的 NPS 和留存？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it was not.
zh: 不，并没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why did fixing onboarding fix the overall sort of customer sat of the end-to-end product?
zh: 那么为什么修复引导问题能修复端到端产品的整体客户满意度？

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought we were solving an onboarding problem, which was overcome the blank page, but it turns out we were discovering product market fit because the real job to be done for the customer is also solve the blank page.
zh: 我们以为自己在解决一个引导问题，也就是克服空白页，但事实证明我们是在发现市场契合，因为客户真正要完成的任务同样是解决空白页。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we solved what we thought was our problem, which was solve the blank page for our onboarding, we actually solved their problem, which was solve the blank page for me to avoid all this time making a presentation.
zh: 于是当我们解决了我们以为是自己的问题——也就是为我们的引导流程解决空白页——我们实际上解决了他们的问题，也就是为我解决空白页，从而省去制作演示文稿的所有这些时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turned out that was actually the thing that had product market fit.
zh: 而事实证明，那才是真正具有市场契合的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you explain more about that?
zh: 你能再多解释一下吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, if you just think about the last time you had to make a presentation,
zh: 从根本上说，只要你想想上一次你必须做演示文稿的时候，

speaker: Unknown
en: And just how that immediately felt to you like, oh shit, big high stakes presentation to the boss, the client, whatever it is, your mind immediately leaps to all the work you have to do.
zh: 以及那立刻给你的感觉，比如，哦糟糕，给老板、给客户或其他什么人的高风险大演示，你的脑子立刻跳到所有你必须做的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to come up with a visual design.
zh: 我得想出一个视觉设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to make a template.
zh: 我得做一个模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to structure the story and pull together all the key ideas.
zh: 我得组织故事结构，并把所有关键想法汇集起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to lay out each individual slide and make sure it doesn't overflow off the page.
zh: 我得逐张排版每一页幻灯片，确保内容不会溢出页面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now I need to fill the space.
zh: 而现在我需要填充空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I got to find some stupid clip art and fill it up.
zh: 所以我得找一些愚蠢的剪贴画来填满它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're suddenly looking at like 10 hours of work to make anything good minimum.
zh: 你突然面对的是至少 10 个小时的工作才能做出任何像样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every time you're almost restarting, not to mention the fragility of like your team starts to edit and mess with it.
zh: 而且每次都几乎是重新开始，更不用说那种脆弱性，比如你的团队开始编辑、乱改它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we did was we just eliminated maybe eight or nine of those 10 hours right off the board.
zh: 于是我们做的就是把那 10 个小时中的大概八到九个小时直接消掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you can give that concrete a time savings, the value is just so immediate concrete and people left on it.
zh: 当你能给出这样具体的时间节省时，价值就是如此即时和具体，人们为此留下。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you were working on onboarding, did you think it could solve the entire sort of basically how satisfying this product is?
zh: 当你在做引导流程时，你有没有想过它能解决产品的整个基本满意度问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not originally, that's not what we prioritized it, but we have a strong dogfooding culture.
zh: 一开始没有，我们并不是把它作为优先事项，但我们有很强的 dogfooding（自用）文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're using our own product every single day.
zh: 我们每天都在使用自己的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember this moment, maybe a month or so into this three-month sprint to get this big new AI version of our product, where we were all just sitting around at lunch, playing with a mobile version of our product, and we started just making presentations about anything we could think of, you know, like different breeds of cats.
zh: 我记得有这么一个时刻，大概是在为期三个月的冲刺、要做出我们产品的大规模新 AI 版本的一个月左右，我们大家在午餐时坐在一起，玩着我们产品的移动版本，我们开始就任何能想到的东西做演示文稿，比如不同品种的猫。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why does Subway smell so good?
zh: 为什么 Subway 闻起来这么香？

speaker: Unknown
en: All these kinds of questions.
zh: 所有这类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we realized that it was fun in the same way that like a social media app is fun or a game that you play is fun.
zh: 然后我们意识到，它很有趣，就像社交媒体应用那样有趣，或者像你玩的游戏那样有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was this new kind of dopamine reward that you got from generating these things.
zh: 它是一种新式的多巴胺奖励，你从生成这些东西中获得。

speaker: Unknown
en: And suddenly I got this inkling of, whoa, this could actually be a whole product value proposition.
zh: 突然间我有了这样一种预感，哇，这实际上可能是一个完整的产品价值主张。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this aspect of like the slot machine of what am I going to get?
zh: 它有这种老虎机的成分，就是我会得到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you think about building the product for a specific subset of presentation creators and sort of were trying to work backwards from that and sort of bound the jobs to be done?
zh: 你有没有想过为演示文稿创作者的某个特定子集构建产品，并试图从那个方向倒推、框定要完成的任务？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or did you think very generically about a generalizable tool that anybody to do anything could use?
zh: 还是你非常通用地去思考一个可泛化的工具，任何人用它做任何事都可以？

speaker: Unknown
en: We bet early on and pretty consistently on building a horizontal product rather than a vertical one that was focused on a specific persona.
zh: 我们很早就、并且相当一致地押注于打造一个横向产品，而不是一个聚焦于特定人群画像的纵向产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was actually a source of constant tension in fundraising and a lot of our early debates, because I think there's sort of a playbook out there, which is you need to pick a very narrow vertical, satisfy that customer type, and then build outwards from there.
zh: 这实际上是融资过程中持续紧张的一个来源，也是我们很多早期争论的焦点，因为我认为外面有一种现成的打法，就是你需要选一个非常窄的纵向领域，满足那类客户，然后从那里向外扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bet against that because we looked at this productivity space and all the most inspiring companies that we saw were not verticalized in this way.
zh: 我们反其道而行，因为我们看了生产力这个领域，我们见到的所有最令人振奋的公司都不是这样纵向化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were actually quite horizontal.
zh: 它们实际上相当横向。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your notions, your slacks, your looms.
zh: 比如你的 Notion、你的 Slack、你的 Loom。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually difficult to pin down where their early fit had come from.
zh: 实际上，很难确定他们早期的契合点是从哪里来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could do it in some cases.
zh: 在某些情况下你能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe slack was early stage startups or whatever it is.
zh: 也许 Slack 是早期初创公司，或者诸如此类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these companies were fairly broad in who they targeted.
zh: 但这些公司针对的目标人群相当宽泛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if they had a persona, it wasn't a single narrow type.
zh: 即使他们有一个用户画像，也不是单一狭窄的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a broad one.
zh: 而是一个宽泛的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually settled on a broad one, which was external presenting, not like the internal company at all hands, but somebody in a role like sales or marketing or consulting who is ultimately trying to get business from somebody else.
zh: 所以我们最终确定的是一个宽泛的画像，那就是对外展示，不是公司内部的全员大会那种，而是像销售、市场营销或咨询这类角色的人，他们最终是要从别人那里争取业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there was natural virality to it.
zh: 因为它有天然的自传播性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would spread between organizations.
zh: 它会在组织之间传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was natural willingness to pay because the presentation was ultimately tied to some kind of revenue generating activity for that business.
zh: 而且人们有天然的付费意愿，因为演示文稿最终是和该业务的某种创收活动挂钩的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've always kind of leaned towards that direction while still being good for other use cases like internal presentations.
zh: 所以我们一直偏向这个方向，同时对其他用例比如内部演示也做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we chose not to narrow any further.
zh: 但我们选择不再进一步收窄。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that served us well, at least up to this point, because we've proven that with that broad product, you can serve a huge horizontal user base.
zh: 我认为这一点对我们很有帮助，至少到目前为止是这样，因为我们已经证明了，凭借这个宽泛的产品，你可以服务一个巨大的横向用户群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that a very easy decision or did you spend real time sort of working through it?
zh: 这是个很容易的决定吗？还是说你花了真功夫去反复琢磨？

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, it actually always felt easy.
zh: 对我来说，其实一直觉得很轻松。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was obvious just looking at the leading tools in the space that that was the path that they had taken.
zh: 只要看看这个领域里那些领先的工具，就很明显他们走的就是这条路。

speaker: Unknown
en: A tool like PowerPoint is not a vertical solution, it's horizontal.
zh: 像 PowerPoint 这样的工具不是垂直解决方案，它是横向的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was a source of constant friction because I would say every investor asked us about it and challenged us on it, which then caused us to question ourselves over and over.
zh: 但这是一个持续摩擦的来源，因为可以说，每一位投资人都问过我们这个问题，并且就此挑战过我们，这又让我们一次次地怀疑自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you think about, and do you currently think about building the product as if you are building a consumer product company?
zh: 你们有没有想过——以及现在是否在考虑——把产品当作一个消费级产品公司来打造？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think overall we've leaned consumer, especially early on.
zh: 我认为总体上我们偏向消费级，尤其是在早期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just give some concrete ways in which we have looked more consumer-like.
zh: 也许举一些具体的例子，说明我们在哪些方面看起来更像消费级公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The composition of our team early on, you know, our original team, we had product market fit, was 12 people, of which zero were in any kind of GTM role, so we had no sales or marketing.
zh: 我们早期团队的组成，你知道，我们最初的团队，也就是我们实现产品市场契合时的团队，是 12 个人，其中没有任何一个担任 GTM 类角色的，所以我们没有销售也没有市场营销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Four out of those 12 were UX designers.
zh: 这 12 个人里有 4 个是 UX 设计师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's actually a pretty insane ratio of one-third.
zh: 所以这实际上是个相当疯狂的比例，三分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's the kind of ratio you do when you're a consumer company who's betting on...
zh: 但这就是当你是一家消费级公司、押注于……时才会采用的比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: User experience and product-led growth being your main driver.
zh: 用户体验和产品驱动增长是你主要的驱动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think another example is that we've relied heavily on techniques like A-B testing, coming from my kind of Optimizely heritage, to iterate our way towards everything from pricing to AI models to user experience.
zh: 我想另一个例子是，我们大量依赖 A/B 测试这样的技术——这源于我那种 Optimizely 出身的背景——用迭代的方式打磨一切，从定价到 AI 模型再到用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also generally a much more consumer-skewed technique.
zh: 这总体上也是一种更偏向消费级的技术手段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one thing that informed this orientation was actually the very first exercise we did when we started the company.
zh: 我认为，塑造了这个方向的一件事，实际上是我们创办公司时做的第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before anything else, before we built any product, was we did 100 user interviews, and we used to ask people in different walks of life, different verticals basically, tell me the last time you made a presentation.
zh: 在其他任何事之前，在我们构建任何产品之前，我们做了 100 场用户访谈，我们问不同行业、不同阶层的人：告诉我你上一次做演示文稿是什么时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was that like?
zh: 那是怎样的体验？

speaker: Unknown
en: We had them walk through what they made, how they made it, what went well and what didn't go well.
zh: 我们让他们 walkthrough 他们做了什么、怎么做的、哪些顺利哪些不顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the really extraordinary thing from doing that exercise was hearing that of those 100 people,
zh: 而做这件事真正非同寻常的一点是，我们听到这 100 个人里，

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether they were a consultant or a teacher or a doctor or a tech employee, they all said pretty much the exact same stuff.
zh: 无论他们是咨询师、老师、医生还是科技公司员工，他们说的几乎完全是同样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't that the doctor had different presentation needs than the consultant by and large.
zh: 总体而言，并不是医生和咨询师有不同的演示需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were some specifics.
zh: 虽然有一些具体差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was almost all the same few problems, which is actually this blank page problem.
zh: 几乎全都是同样那几个问题，实际上就是这个空白页问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know where to start.
zh: 我不知道从哪里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: This feeling of judgment.
zh: 这种被评判的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like people are judging me based on how my slides look, not what I'm trying to say.
zh: 我感觉人们在根据我的幻灯片外观评判我，而不是我想表达的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this huge tax of formatting.
zh: 然后还有排版这个巨大的税负。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spend all this time just moving boxes around to align them and make them look right.
zh: 我花了所有这些时间只是把一个个框移来移去对齐，让它们看起来正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the quotes we heard, probably the single most common quote we heard from all these people, no matter what their job was,
zh: 我们听到的很多引述，可能是从所有这些人那里听到的最常见的一句，无论他们的工作是什么，

speaker: Unknown
en: was I spend 90% of my time on formatting and 10% of my time on content.
zh: 都是：我把 90% 的时间花在排版上，只有 10% 的时间花在内容上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so unlocking that, flipping that ratio became kind of the skeleton key that felt totally horizontal, not vertical to one specific user type.
zh: 所以解锁这一点，把这个比例翻转过来，就成了那把万能钥匙，感觉完全是横向的，不是针对某一类特定用户的垂直需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about how you went from that to sort of this prototyping motion.
zh: 谈谈你们是怎么从那个阶段走到这种原型制作的做法的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we started with those user problems.
zh: 是的，我们从那些用户问题出发。

speaker: Unknown
en: We boiled it down to three top ones, which was basically like, you know, formatting, structure, and content.
zh: 我们把它归结为三大问题，基本上就是，你知道，排版、结构和内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we dove into prototyping.
zh: 然后我们就一头扎进了原型制作。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of our early team were either designer, engineer types, so everybody was capable of building things.
zh: 我们早期团队都是设计师、工程师类型的人，所以每个人都有能力构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keep in mind, this is pre-AI coding, so we still had to do it all the old-fashioned way, hand-rolled by hand.
zh: 记住，这是在 AI 编程出现之前，所以我们还是得用老式的方式，全部手工打造。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we built a ton of prototypes.
zh: 但我们做了大量的原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would build multiple every week.
zh: 我们每周会做多个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would take them back to some of those same users.
zh: 我们会把它们带回给那些同样的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really relied heavily on trying these things ourselves.
zh: 我们非常依赖自己试用这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on, these products were all so bad, you could barely even ask a customer to make a presentation in them because presentations are naturally high stakes.
zh: 早期，这些产品都非常糟糕，你几乎没法让客户用它做演示，因为演示天然是高风险的。

speaker: Unknown
en: People use them for real work.
zh: 人们用它做真正的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product wasn't ready for real work.
zh: 产品当时还没准备好应对真正的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we made presentations ourselves over and over every day.
zh: 所以我们自己一遍又一遍地、每天做演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the fact that you had weak product market fit ended up being a huge lucky break in that if the company had much stronger product market fit, it would be harder to rebuild it when these new AI primitives sort of were invented?
zh: 你是否认为，你们产品市场契合度较弱这件事最终反而成了一个巨大的幸运转机——因为如果当时公司的产品市场契合度强得多，那么当这些新的 AI 原语被发明出来时，重建它就会更难？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, I absolutely feel that way.
zh: 是的，我绝对这么觉得。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in many ways we got extraordinarily lucky by having built so much of the non-AI primitives and infrastructure that gave us something to build upon, but not being wedded to any of it and knowing we had to make a lot of changes at the moment AI came along.
zh: 我认为在很多方面我们非常幸运，因为我们已经构建了大量非 AI 的原语和基础设施，让我们有了可以依托的东西，但又不拘泥于其中任何一部分，并且知道在 AI 到来之时我们必须做出很多改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we could throw out the parts that weren't serving us, but we weren't building from zero.
zh: 所以我们可以扔掉那些对我们没用的部分，但我们不是从零开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We weren't building a pure GPT wrapper, so to speak, because we actually had years of technology we'd built up that AI could layer on top of.
zh: 可以说，我们不是在做一个纯粹的 GPT 套壳，因为我们实际上有多年来积累的技术，AI 可以叠加在其之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's an interesting challenge now because as we grow, you know, product market fit is not guaranteed.
zh: 现在这成了一个有趣的挑战，因为随着我们成长，你知道，产品市场契合度并不是有保障的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get to just keep it because you had it before.
zh: 你不能因为以前拥有它就一直保留它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in this incredibly competitive space.
zh: 我们身处这个竞争极其激烈的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we have the challenge that we have been so successful.
zh: 但现在我们面临的挑战是，我们已经如此成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have more than 100 million users who have signed up for our product.
zh: 我们有超过 1 亿用户注册了我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But AI has not slowed down.
zh: 但 AI 并没有放慢速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anything, it's sped up.
zh: 如果说有什么变化的话，它是加速了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're having to now think very carefully about how we chuck out parts of our product we have today and embrace new ones while managing that larger legacy base.
zh: 所以我们现在必须非常仔细地思考，如何舍弃我们今天产品中的某些部分、拥抱新的部分，同时管理好这个庞大的存量用户基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do that?
zh: 你是怎么做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what does that sound like?
zh: 就是说，那听起来是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It means constantly questioning some of our core design principles, a lot of bets that we made early on.
zh: 它意味着不断质疑我们的一些核心设计原则，以及我们早期做出的很多押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Gemma's early success came in this period, 2023, when LLMs weren't very good yet.
zh: 你知道，Gemma 的早期成功是在那个时期到来的，2023 年，当时 LLM 还不是很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of what made our product great was guardrails we put around these kind of dumb, they weren't even agents yet, dumb prompts to protect the AI from itself.
zh: 所以让我们的产品变得出色的很多东西，是我们围绕这些有点笨的——它们当时甚至还不是智能体——笨提示词设置的护栏，用来保护 AI 不被自己坑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now what we're finding actually is that all those guardrails we put in place are holding these much more intelligent AIs back.
zh: 而现在我们实际上发现，我们设下的所有那些护栏，正在拖累这些聪明得多的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're now in a mode not of even adding functionality but trying to throw things out, loosen the requirements, and let AI do more overall.
zh: 所以我们现在处于一种模式，甚至不是在增加功能，而是试图把东西扔出去，放宽要求，让 AI 总体上做更多的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Knowing what you know now about the path of the company and kind of the way that the product was reinvented, do you think everything unfolded how it needed to?
zh: 根据你现在对这家公司的发展路径以及产品被重塑的方式的了解，你认为一切都以它需要的方式展开了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or could it have been done faster or differently?
zh: 还是说本可以更快或以不同的方式完成？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think you can always look back with hindsight and say we should have skipped that route of the idea maze and gone straight to the good idea, but that's not really possible.
zh: 嗯，我想你总是可以带着后见之明回望，说我们应该跳过那条想法迷宫的路线，直接走向好点子，但这其实是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you don't have the time machine.
zh: 是啊，你没有时间机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I guess your question is more like if you were just to execute again with sort of laser-like focus, could you have gotten there more quickly and more directly?
zh: 不过我猜你的问题更像是，如果只是以某种激光般的专注度重新执行一遍，能否更快、更直接地到达那里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for sure, yes.
zh: 我觉得肯定是可以的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took some wrong turns and those wrong turns are still kind of embedded in the DNA of our product in many ways.
zh: 我们走过一些弯路，而这些弯路在很多方面至今仍嵌在我们产品的 DNA 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the work of...
zh: 很多工作是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Scaling through this next stage of growth is figuring out which of those wrong turns to undo.
zh: 跨越下一个增长阶段，就是搞清楚哪些弯路需要撤销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, which of those were not really wrong turns, they were just too early and seeds of something greater.
zh: 还有，哪些其实并不是真正的弯路，它们只是太早了，是某种更伟大事物的种子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, there are some aspects of our product which never hit product market fit in that early stage, but I think still could actually.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们产品的某些方面在那个早期阶段从未达到产品市场契合，但我认为实际上将来仍有可能达到。

speaker: Unknown
en: To give a simple example, one of the early bets that Gamma took was interactivity.
zh: 举一个简单的例子，Gamma 早期押注之一是交互性。

speaker: Unknown
en: This idea that a presentation didn't have to be just a linear narrative where you click through slide by slide.
zh: 这个想法是，演示不必只是逐张点击幻灯片的线性叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But instead you could have live interactive elements on the screen.
zh: 而是可以在屏幕上放置实时的交互元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on that turned out not to resonate with our first product market fit because people really just wanted to interoperate with the world they're used to of make traditional PowerPoints.
zh: 早期，这一点被证明无法与我们的第一个产品市场契合产生共鸣，因为人们真的只想与他们所习惯的世界互通——制作传统的 PowerPoint。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they actually caused all this pain for us of trying to figure out how to bridge this interactivity with this legacy format that was not interactive.
zh: 所以这实际上给我们带来了所有这些痛苦，即试图把这种交互性与这个不支持交互的传统格式衔接起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're still facing that pain because...
zh: 而我们至今仍在面对那种痛苦，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in kind of this crossing the chasm period where we're trying to win over people that want familiarity.
zh: 我们正处于某种跨越鸿沟的时期，我们试图赢下那些想要熟悉感的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as we grow our distribution and become a platform in our own right where people spend time, now we can actually reintroduce those elements and they become actually part of the stickiness of why someone wants to stay in a tool like Gamma versus exporting to somewhere else.
zh: 但随着我们扩展分发渠道、成为一个人们愿意花时间的独立平台，现在我们实际上可以重新引入那些元素，而它们会成为用户想留在 Gamma 这样的工具里而不是导出到别处的粘性的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so many of these concepts have a proper time, but I think looking back as a founder, a lot of the mistakes come from misjudging timing versus misjudging ideas.
zh: 所以这些概念中有很多都有其合适的时间，但我觉得作为创始人回望，很多错误来自于误判时机，而不是误判想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more about that.
zh: 多说说这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think as a first-time founder, a lot of my naivete came from looking at some product and saying, I can make it better.
zh: 我想作为第一次创业的人，我的很多天真来自于看着某个产品然后说，我能做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that might be true, but I think there's a couple false assumptions that live inside that declaration of better.
zh: 这可能是真的，但我觉得在这个「更好」的宣言里藏着几个错误的假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is that just because I think it's better doesn't mean the user think it's better.
zh: 第一个是，仅仅因为我认为它更好，并不意味着用户认为它更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the other one is thinking about the user in isolation versus the system in which they operate.
zh: 但另一个是，把用户孤立地看待，而不是把他们所处的系统放在一起考虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with productivity, you're always collaborating with peers.
zh: 而在生产力这件事上，你总是在和同伴协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have work guidelines and templates you have to follow.
zh: 你有必须遵守的工作规范和模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of our best ideas were, what if you could be free of all of that?
zh: 所以我们的很多最好的想法是，如果你能摆脱所有这些会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: But people are not free of all that.
zh: 但人们并不能摆脱所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to meet them where they are.
zh: 所以你必须在他们所在的地方迎接他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to bridge that familiarity gap.
zh: 你必须弥合那种熟悉感的鸿沟。

speaker: Unknown
en: And only once you've bridged it and started to bring people into your new system can you now start to layer on what you really thought was magical about the vision.
zh: 而且只有在你弥合了这个鸿沟、开始把人们带进你的新系统之后，你才能开始叠加你当初真正觉得这个愿景有魔力的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you really see this with companies that have been in this game much longer than we have at Gamma.
zh: 而且我觉得你在那些比我们在 Gamma 玩这个游戏久得多的公司身上真的能看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm thinking again about these companies that inspire us, like a Slack or a Notion or a Canva.
zh: 我又想到了这些启发我们的公司，比如 Slack、Notion 或 Canva。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on, they all took different spins on the thing they were replacing, like docs and email.
zh: 早期，它们对自己要取代的东西——比如文档和邮件——都采取了不同的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some parts of it were unfamiliar and confusing, and they had to layer in those sort of bridges to make sense.
zh: 其中一些部分是陌生和令人困惑的，它们不得不加入那些桥梁来让它说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now that these companies have all been around for, let's say, 10 years, they're getting to really dig into those original parts of their vision and bring them to life.
zh: 但现在这些公司都已经存在了大概十年，它们得以真正深入挖掘它们愿景中最初的部分，并将其变为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the things that you would have done differently knowing everything that you know, there's a huge chunk of it which is at that time it was just unknowable.
zh: 如果你想想那些你带着现在所知的一切会以不同方式去做的事，其中有很大一部分在当时是完全不可知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that case, the way that you work through the idea maze is required or you couldn't unearth it.
zh: 在这种情况下，你穿越想法迷宫的方式是必需的，否则你无法把它发掘出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other is from time to time, there are things actually that were totally knowable at that time, but because of your own frame of reference or all sorts of other things, you went in the wrong direction.
zh: 另一种情况是，偶尔也确实有一些事情在当时是完全可知的，但由于你自己的参照框架或其他种种原因，你走错了方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious if in that second bucket, if there are any specific things that come to mind that were important or did it tended to be more, it was unknowable, we had to sort of go down the hallway, realize the door was closed, then go to sort of, you know, another door.
zh: 我很好奇在第二类里，有没有什么具体的、浮现在脑海中的重要事情，还是说更多的情况是——那是不可知的，我们不得不沿着走廊走，发现门是关着的，然后再走向另一扇门。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest one that comes to mind for me is the kind of obvious and hindsight realization that, you know, we had started by trying to pioneer this new creative format that was somewhere in between presentation, document, webpage.
zh: 对我来说想到的最大一个，是那种事后显而易见的领悟，就是，我们一开始是试图开创这种介于演示文稿、文档、网页之间的新创意格式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was mobile responsive, content would adjust and reflow.
zh: 所以它是移动端自适应的，内容会调整和重排。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was what created a lot of our early propulsion, which was that this format actually worked really nicely for LLMs.
zh: 而这正是我们早期很多推进力的来源，那就是这种格式其实对 LLM 非常好用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the blind spot for us, though, was drinking our own Kool-Aid that people always want to operate in our new format versus the sort of obvious realization that, no, everybody is still exporting this thing to PowerPoint early on because that's where their team lives.
zh: 不过我觉得我们的盲点在于，喝了自己灌的迷魂汤，以为人们总是想在我们的新格式里操作，而忽略了那个显而易见的领悟，就是，不，早期每个人仍然在把这个东西导出到 PowerPoint，因为那是他们团队所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we did build a PowerPoint export, but probably a year too late.
zh: 所以我们确实做了 PowerPoint 导出，但大概晚了一年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we should have listened to the signals earlier on of people just telling us this is what they wanted.
zh: 我觉得我们应该更早地听取人们直接告诉我们这就是他们想要的那些信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we were kind of so excited about our own format and wanting to build our own proprietary frame of reference.
zh: 但我们当时对自己的格式太兴奋了，一心想打造自己的专有参照框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: This also, I think, came from perhaps trying to build for durability in moat before building for adoption.
zh: 我想这也可能来自于，先为持久性和护城河而建，而不是先为采用而建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you actually have to go in the opposite order.
zh: 而我觉得你其实必须按相反的顺序来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to first win adoption, which is a kind of a grueling fight with someone who is changing their workflow and only then build some of that stickiness around it.
zh: 你必须先赢得采用，这是一场和一个正在改变自己工作流程的人之间的艰苦战斗，然后才能围绕它建立一些粘性。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things you're sort of touching on, and I think it's really interesting in sort of a consumer or prosumer sort of form factor of software, is you have sort of a lot of people that say the way to build products is just to build the thing that you would want.
zh: 你在某种程度上触及到的一件事，我觉得在那种消费级或半消费级形态的软件里非常有趣，就是有很多人说，做产品的方法就是做你自己想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're the customer.
zh: 你就是客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's another version of it, which is, no, you have to get really close to customers.
zh: 还有另一个版本，就是，不，你必须非常贴近客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And understand what they care about or not necessarily have them design the product, but have them articulate their problems.
zh: 并且理解他们在乎什么，不一定是让他们设计产品，而是让他们把问题讲清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's some, maybe some place in between, but there's definitely like a customer centric worldview.
zh: 然后还有一些，也许介于两者之间，但肯定有一种以客户为中心的世界观。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then maybe there's like the Jobsian worldview, which is like.
zh: 然后也许还有那种 Jobs 式的世界观，就是——

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to sort of instantiate the thing you've always wanted.
zh: 你必须把你一直想要的东西实现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like in the in the journey of Gamma, there's been this sort of connection between these two because there's this dogfooding culture.
zh: 而在 Gamma 的历程里，感觉这两者之间一直存在这种联系，因为有一种内部试用文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this the whole company was started around wanting a thing that didn't exist.
zh: 整个公司就是围绕着想要一个不存在的东西而创立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What else could you sort of reflect on sort of those two maybe worldviews?
zh: 关于这两种也许的世界观，你还能反思些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's really well put.
zh: 我觉得你说得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like we've constantly been sailing between these worldviews.
zh: 而且我感觉我们一直在这两种世界观之间航行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I would ally us with either one purely.
zh: 我不认为我们会纯粹地归属于其中任何一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're right that we have had this sort of Jobsian mindset of build the thing that didn't already exist.
zh: 我觉得你说得对，我们确实有过那种 Jobs 式的心态，去打造一个之前不存在的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't quite know what they're asking for.
zh: 人们并不完全知道自己想要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in the early stages, you see that in the way that we started from problems.
zh: 而且我觉得在早期，你能从我们始于问题的方式中看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really make sure we're aligned with the customer on the problems that they're stating, but show them a solution that is not necessarily what they wanted.
zh: 真正确保我们在客户所陈述的问题上与他们对齐，但展示给他们的解决方案不一定是他们想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I also alluded to, there were times where we drank our own Kool-Aid too much and we believed we had built the 10x better solution, when really the customer was telling us, nah, I actually want this other thing instead.
zh: 但正如我也提到过的，有些时候我们喝自己的迷魂汤喝得太多，我们相信自己做出了好 10 倍的解决方案，而实际上客户在告诉我们，不，我其实想要的是另外那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've gone through periods of having to then re-anchor that against exactly what customers are telling us.
zh: 所以我们经历过一些时期，不得不重新以客户确切告诉我们的内容为锚点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're really experiencing this now as we take our consumery product and go into B2B, where in many ways there's already product market fit.
zh: 我们现在真的正在经历这一点,因为我们把面向消费者的产品带入 B2B,而在很多方面那里已经有了产品市场契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are kind of using this thing undercover, they're pulling it into their companies, but at the same time we're hitting brick walls on certain aspects of the product that need to change because businesses have very different needs than consumers.
zh: 人们在某种程度上是在「暗地里」使用这个东西,他们把它拉进自己的公司,但与此同时,我们在产品的某些方面撞上了砖墙,需要做出改变,因为企业的需求与消费者非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say as a leader, it's been on my mind how to cultivate both mindsets, especially when it comes to like our design team, which needs to both contain this research stay close to the customer mindset, but also this kind of maverick creative buildup thing they haven't asked for yet mindset.
zh: 我想说的是,作为一名领导者,如何培养这两种心态一直在我脑海中,尤其是涉及到我们的设计团队时,他们既需要保持这种贴近客户的研究心态,也需要保持那种「先发型」的创意积累——做他们还没主动要求的东西——的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's your best cut at that?
zh: 那么,你对此最好的切入点是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if you are trying to indoctrinate that into the people designing products, building products, engineering products, how does it manifest itself?
zh: 或者,如果你正试图把这种理念灌输给那些设计产品、构建产品、工程化产品的人,它会以什么形式体现出来?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the quote that I heard about this that I have always really liked is that you diagnose with data and solve with design.
zh: 你知道,我听到的关于这个的一句话,我一直非常喜欢,那就是:用数据做诊断,用设计做解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I take that to mean is, first of all, when it comes to quantitative data, we try to be a very data-driven organization.
zh: 我对此的理解是,首先,在量化数据方面,我们努力成为一个非常数据驱动的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really stick to metrics and analytics and A-B testing, but there's also qualitative data.
zh: 我们非常坚持指标、分析和 A/B 测试,但也有定性数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We try to always stay very close to what the customer is telling us and let us all kind of marinate in that.
zh: 我们努力始终非常贴近客户告诉我们的东西,让我们大家都沉浸其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're not gonna give us solutions.
zh: 但他们不会给我们解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way to actually solve solutions is to get out ahead of those problems
zh: 真正解决的方式是要走在这些问题的前面,

speaker: Unknown
en: and find the unlock whether it's a UX designer making a mock-up but even more often now it's an engineer actually prototyping something with AI that sometimes crystallizes or unlocks three or four different problems we've heard into one new solution and then bounce back and forth and diagnose did this actually solve the problem?
zh: 并找到那个解法,无论是 UX 设计师做一个原型图,但更常见的是现在由工程师用 AI 对某个东西做原型,这有时会把我们听到的三四个不同的问题结晶或解锁成一个新方案,然后来回反复,诊断这是否真的解决了问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's shove this in people's faces and let them tell us where it holds up and where it doesn't.
zh: 让我们把这个东西怼到人们面前,让他们告诉我们哪里站得住脚,哪里站不住脚。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about sort of the episodic nature of the product?
zh: 你是如何思考这个产品那种「偶发性」的特性的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say it is the biggest structural challenge with this category.
zh: 我想说,这是这个品类最大的结构性挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: You also you didn't mention another structural challenge, which is that competitors are all bundled into larger suites.
zh: 你还——你也没提到另一个结构性挑战,那就是竞争对手都被捆绑进更大的套件里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was going to say, yeah, there's generally, I would imagine, low willingness to pay.
zh: 我正想说,是的,总体来说,我猜,付费意愿会比较低。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think these two factors are why this category of presentations has been a graveyard of startups.
zh: 我认为这两个因素就是为什么这个演示品类一直是初创公司的坟场。

speaker: Unknown
en: PowerPoint came out in 1987, and in the last 39 years, basically nobody else has managed to unseat them.
zh: PowerPoint 在 1987 年问世,在过去的 39 年里,基本上没有其他公司成功地把他们拉下马。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies that have come closest, you know, you probably say Google Slides and maybe Keynote.
zh: 最接近的那些公司,你可能会说 Google Slides,或者还有 Keynote。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not even really serious competitors.
zh: 他们甚至算不上真正的竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were ports of the same product to different platforms as part of a different larger suite.
zh: 他们只是同一产品向不同平台的移植,作为另一个更大套件的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this was always our biggest doubt and fear about entering the category and probably our, again, naivete that we even did it at all.
zh: 所以这一直是我们进入这个品类时最大的疑虑和恐惧,也可能——再说了——我们居然真的进了,这本身就是我们的天真。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think what we felt was that these dynamics created stagnation in the category and that stagnation was what made room for a disruptor to come with the right why now.
zh: 但我认为我们当时的感受是,这些动态造成了这个品类的停滞,而这种停滞正是为一个带着正确的「为什么是现在」的颠覆者留出了空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were actually wrong about the why now.
zh: 其实我们关于「为什么是现在」的判断是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought it was remote work and COVID.
zh: 我们以为是远程办公和疫情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got lucky that a better why now came along just in time, which was AI, and really embraced that.
zh: 我们很幸运,一个更好的「为什么是现在」恰逢其时地出现了,那就是 AI,我们也真正拥抱了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And AI is such a sea change that I do think it is just this anti-income technology across the board.
zh: 而 AI 是如此巨大的剧变,我确实认为它就是一种全面的「反收入」技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is, I mean, this is why we have a SaaSpocalypse now, is it's kind of questioning every software company's moat.
zh: 我是说,这就是为什么我们现在有一场「SaaS 大末日」,因为它在质疑每一家软件公司的护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what's given us, let's say, the boldness to be a challenger in this category, despite those challenges.
zh: 所以,正是这一点给了我们——可以这么说——做这个品类挑战者的胆量,尽管有那些挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: I won't claim that we've solved all those problems.
zh: 我不会声称我们已经解决了所有这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are iterating through them.
zh: 我们正在其中迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although I do think probably what's been most valuable to us is to have the mindset of being okay with a broad, horizontal, somewhat episodic user base because we believe we can find pockets of deep value inside of that.
zh: 不过我确实认为,对我们最有价值的,可能是保持这样一种心态:接受一个广泛的、水平化的、 somewhat 偶发性的用户群体,因为我们相信我们能在其中找到深度价值的 pockets。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not an either or.
zh: 而这不是二选一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not build the horizontal product or build the sort of like verticalized solution with depth for a different customer base.
zh: 不是要么做水平化产品,要么做那种为不同客户群体提供深度的垂直化解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit more T-shaped.
zh: 它更像是 T 字形的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've started with that wide horizontal base, which is still growing just given this kind of tidal wave of change coming from AI.
zh: 我们从那个宽的水平化基座开始,而它仍在增长,因为这股来自 AI 的变化浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we think we can build pillars of depth within that.
zh: 但我们认为我们可以在此基础上建起深度支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're already seeing signs of that, particularly in our B2B motion, our API.
zh: 我们已经看到了这方面的迹象,尤其是在我们的 B2B 动作、我们的 API 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what's different about those is they represent repeated workflows on teams rather than episodic usage by individuals.
zh: 我认为这些的不同之处在于,它们代表的是团队上重复的工作流,而不是个体的偶发性使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the challenge our team is trying to navigate is how to keep growing that prosumer user base while also building those pillars of depth.
zh: 所以我们团队正在努力应对的挑战是,如何一边持续增长那个 prosumer 用户群体,一边构建那些深度支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what's kind of your best crack at that now?
zh: 那么你目前对此最好的破解方式是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think our best crack at it where we've already seen such clear value is when you have a larger company, so not these small prosumer use cases, but companies of thousands of people or even, you know, Fortune 10s or Fortune 100s with tens of thousands of people.
zh: 我认为我们最好的破解方式——我们已经看到了如此明确的价值的地方——是当你有一家更大的公司,不是这些小型的 prosumer 用例,而是几千人的公司,甚至你知道的,财富前十或财富一百强那种几万人的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where they have some team at their company that has a repeated presentation use case.
zh: 他们公司里有一些团队有重复性的演示用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most obvious one you can think of is like a sales team where you've got people just pitching the product over and over and over again in a fairly repeated and templated way.
zh: 你能想到的最明显的一个就是销售团队,那里的人们以相当重复和模板化的方式一遍又一遍地推介产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can think of it as almost following a recipe over and over again.
zh: 你几乎可以把它想成是一遍又一遍地照着一个菜谱做菜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And where we have now rolled out a B2B offering as well as an API with connectors into common tools.
zh: 而我们现在已经推出了 B2B 产品,以及一个带连接器、接入常用工具的 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a simple example to think about is that sales team uses, let's say, Salesforce as their CRM system of record.
zh: 举个简单的例子来理解:那个销售团队使用,比如说,Salesforce 作为他们的 CRM 记录系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And any time an opportunity gets created or advances stages or has a meeting, we can automatically create a presentation based on that, building on all the content that's already happened and hand deliver it to the sales rep to use in the next meeting.
zh: 每当一个商机被创建、推进阶段或有一个会议时,我们就可以基于此自动创建一个演示文稿,建立在已有的全部内容之上,并直接交付给销售代表,供其在下一次会议中使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And companies love that because frankly they don't trust their own sales reps to make good content.
zh: 而公司们很喜欢这一点,因为坦率地说,他们不信任自己的销售代表能做出好的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had a very fragile workflow before of copy-pasting templates.
zh: 他们之前有一套非常脆弱的流程,就是复制粘贴模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we can really streamline that workflow and turn it into a repeated one, we're seeing that there's a huge opportunity in these companies to do it.
zh: 如果我们能真正把这个流程精简化,把它变成一个可重复的流程,我们看到这些公司里存在着巨大的机会去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that...
zh: 那这如何……

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of foot with the nature of this product, which is one that just has infinite roadmap.
zh: 如何与这个产品的特性相契合,也就是一个路线图无限的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You talk to 25 different customers, you know, certain things bubble up, but you could build infinitely because of the form factor of the product.
zh: 你跟 25 个不同的客户聊,你知道,有些东西会浮现出来,但由于产品的形态,你其实可以无限地构建下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you think about either the different chapters of the company's life, how did you think about prioritizing?
zh: 所以当你思考公司生命周期的不同阶段时,你是怎么考虑优先级排序的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, one thing that has both helped us and hurt us in prioritization is being an exceptionally lean company.
zh: 嗯,在优先级排序上,有件事既帮了我们,也坑了我们,那就是我们是一家极其精简的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have generally had a pretty small team.
zh: 我们通常保持着相当小的团队规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a while, we were at over 2 million ARR per employee, which actually felt like too much.
zh: 有一段时间,我们达到了人均超过 200 万美元的 ARR,这实际上感觉有点过头了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like almost comically outsized in terms of the amount of work we had to do versus the size of our team.
zh: 就工作量相对于团队规模而言,几乎夸张到有些滑稽。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it forced a lot of clarity in prioritization.
zh: 但它迫使我们在优先级上变得非常清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's often helped us do something that is hard for product builders to do, which is build less instead of build more.
zh: 而且我认为这常常帮助我们做到了一件对产品构建者来说很难的事,那就是少构建,而不是多构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And particularly in this world of rapidly advancing AI models, it's actually a really healthy instinct because the less you build as product surface area, the more that the AI can actually fill in in actually the white space.
zh: 特别是在 AI 模型快速进步的这个时代,这其实是一个非常健康的本能,因为你作为产品表面积构建得越少,AI 就越能在实际的空白地带里填补更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Langspace was the problem we started out trying to solve.
zh: Langspace 是我们最初试图解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now it's the thing we're trying to give to these models to let them rip.
zh: 现在它是我们要交给这些模型、让它们放手去干的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're trying to engineer an organization that doesn't build a thousand laundry list features, instead builds strong reusable building blocks that AI can work on top of to provide a lot of the remaining range.
zh: 所以我们正试图打造这样一个组织:不构建上千个清单式的功能,而是构建强大的可复用的积木块,让 AI 能在其之上工作,去覆盖剩余的大部分范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have been some of your reflections on building a product for a use case where the current status quo is people creating very bad presentations?
zh: 对于为一个当前现状就是人们在制作非常糟糕的演示文稿的用例来构建产品,你有哪些反思?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, first of all, it's what made us bet on this category.
zh: 嗯,首先,正是这一点让我们押注了这个品类。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are, I'll contrast it to maybe the world of spreadsheets.
zh: 我想把它和电子表格的世界对比一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Excel is such a dominant tool for spreadsheets and I love Excel.
zh: Excel 在电子表格领域是如此占主导地位的工具,而且我喜欢 Excel。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a great product.
zh: 我认为它是一个很棒的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would not want to compete with Excel, even though I do think there are all these interesting ways you could compete with Excel in the sense that like code is coming along.
zh: 我不会想和 Excel 竞争,尽管我确实认为有很多有趣的方式可以和 Excel 竞争,比如说代码正在崛起。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge is that it's so beloved by the people who use it that I would not have seen personally as a founder the daylight of where I can add that 10x value.
zh: 挑战在于,它太受使用者喜爱了,作为创始人,我个人看不到我能在哪里切入提供那种 10 倍的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: PowerPoint felt so ripe to attack because it doesn't have the same feeling.
zh: PowerPoint 则感觉非常容易被攻击,因为它没有同样的情感。

speaker: Unknown
en: The output undermines people's confidence and the process of making it is so taxing that it felt like there was white space here, even despite the structural challenges of the industry.
zh: 它的产出损害人们的信心,而制作它的过程又如此折磨人,所以即便这个行业存在结构性挑战,也让人感觉这里有空白地带。

speaker: Unknown
en: And why do you think that is?
zh: 那你为什么会觉得是这样?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, at PowerPoint, you have, I think, a bunch of smart people that are trying to do great work.
zh: 比如,你知道,在 PowerPoint,我想有一群聪明人正试图做出优秀的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Google Slides has talented technologists and product builders.
zh: 我认为 Google Slides 也有很有才华的技术人员和产品构建者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what's the working theory as to why it is the way that it was?
zh: 那么,关于它为什么是当初那个样子,你的工作理论是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the same structural challenges that make it hard for a startup to succeed here also give an incumbent no reason to put focus into it.
zh: 我认为,正是那些让初创公司难以在这里成功的结构性挑战,也让在位者没有理由在这个方向上投入精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about who's buying the Google suite or the Microsoft Office suite, nobody's doing it by comparing the feature set of PowerPoint versus Google Slides.
zh: 如果你想想谁在购买 Google 套件或 Microsoft Office 套件,没有人是通过对比 PowerPoint 和 Google Slides 的功能集来做决定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, they're comparing Outlook versus Gmail, and maybe after that, like Word versus Google Slides.
zh: 相反,他们比较的是 Outlook 和 Gmail,也许在那之后,才比较 Word 和 Google Slides。

speaker: Unknown
en: And PowerPoint and Google Slides are afterthoughts in their product roadmap.
zh: 而 PowerPoint 和 Google Slides 在他们的产品路线图里是事后才想起来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It shows up in their prioritization of how they allocate engineering talent, product talent, design talent.
zh: 这体现在他们分配工程人才、产品人才、设计人才的优先级上。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, it also increasingly shows up in how they allocate GPUs, which are the new currency.
zh: 顺便说一句,这也越来越多地体现在他们如何分配 GPU 上,而 GPU 是新的货币。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that I've heard secondhand is that, you know, when Google was thinking about where to put its AI resources, of course, they're gonna throw those at Search, which is its flagship, you know, core product, rather than something like Google Slides, which it can count on being sold for free, whether it does well or not.
zh: 我二手听到的说法是,你知道,当 Google 考虑把它的 AI 资源投放到哪里时,当然,他们会把资源投向搜索,那是它的旗舰、核心产品,而不是像 Google Slides 这样的东西——反正不管做得好不好,它都能被搭着卖出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is the interesting opportunity for us.
zh: 所以这就是我们有趣的 opportunity 机会所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've left this huge UX gap for us that we can go after, but there are still these structural business challenges that we have to solve to make it a successful business around that.
zh: 他们给我们留下了巨大的 UX 空白,我们可以去攻占,但仍然有这些结构性的商业挑战需要我们去解决,才能围绕它建立起一门成功的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you could argue Google Sheets is like an example of this.
zh: 比如你可以说 Google Sheets 就是这方面的一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's not a flagship product.
zh: 它不是一个旗舰产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has tremendous adoption.
zh: 但它有着巨大的采用率。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it feels like Google Sheets is doing a much better job of delivering on the promise than Google Slides is.
zh: 不过感觉 Google Sheets 在兑现承诺方面比 Google Slides 做得好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just like Excel to your point is much more beloved than PowerPoint.
zh: 就像你说的,Excel 也比 PowerPoint 受喜爱得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a lot of times the suite is not sold because of Excel.
zh: 但很多时候,套件并不是因为 Excel 才被卖出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in some ways, I guess, Excel has kind of become Kleenex.
zh: 从某种意义上说,我想,Excel 已经有点变成 Kleenex(纸巾)了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's it's sort of that's an interesting part of also the challenge, like when something just becomes a standard.
zh: 而这也是挑战中有意思的一部分,就是当某个东西变成了标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to divert from that standard too much.
zh: 你不想过多地偏离那个标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's absolutely right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably the biggest difference between the Excel workflow and the PowerPoint workflow is creativity and taste.
zh: 我认为 Excel 工作流和 PowerPoint 工作流之间最大的区别可能就是创造力和品味。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's less objective definition of what good looks like and there's much more room for the user and also the brand to express themselves.
zh: 什么是好的,客观定义更少了,用户和品牌都有大得多的表达空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what makes it a really fun problem for us to work on.
zh: 这正是让我们做起来觉得非常有趣的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also what makes it a much more challenging AI problem to tackle.
zh: 这也是让它成为一个更具挑战性的 AI 问题的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, if you imagine how to write evals for a product like Excel versus a product like PowerPoint, I think it's pretty easy to imagine how to write the Excel ones.
zh: 举例来说,如果你想想象如何为一个像 Excel 这样的产品写评测,对比像 PowerPoint 这样的产品,我想 Excel 的评测很容易想象怎么写。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are the formulas correct?
zh: 公式对不对?

speaker: Unknown
en: If we give it a bunch of inputs and outputs, does it give us the right number at the end?
zh: 如果我们给它一堆输入和输出,它最后给出的数字对不对?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's actually a fairly straightforward problem.
zh: 你看,这其实是一个相当直接的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you now imagine how to do that for PowerPoint, there are these mechanical failures, like did the text get clipped at the bottom of the slide or whatever.
zh: 如果你现在想象如何为 PowerPoint 做这件事,有一些机械性的失败,比如文字是不是在幻灯片底部被裁掉了之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once you get past those, it's a way squishier problem to objectively iterate.
zh: 但一旦越过这些,它就是一个“软”得多的问题,很难客观地迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these products are so horizontal.
zh: 而且这些产品非常横向。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got millions of people using them in different ways.
zh: 有数百万人在以不同的方式使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the scale of PowerPoint and Google Slides, you have hundreds of millions of people using them.
zh: 在 PowerPoint 和 Google Slides 的规模上,有数亿人在使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you start to actually need this difficult quality of taste and creativity.
zh: 所以你实际上开始需要这种难以捉摸的品质——品味和创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while I think there is great engineering talent working on those products, I don't think they have treated them as a place where they put their best designers and people who have that taste.
zh: 虽然我认为有很棒的工程人才在做这些产品,但我不认为他们把这些产品当作放置他们最好的设计师和有品味的人的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a hard thing to exercise inside of a big tech company like that.
zh: 在这样的大型科技公司里,这是一件很难施展的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how have you solved the evals problem or how do you think about it at a philosophical level?
zh: 那么你们是如何解决评测问题的,或者在哲学层面你们是怎么看待它的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I won't claim that we have solved it because it's a really tricky problem for us.
zh: 嗯,我不会声称我们已经解决了它,因为这对我们来说是一个非常棘手的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we view it as more of a data problem.
zh: 我认为我们更多地把它看作一个数据问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we are trying to view this less as an objective function of, is this good or bad?
zh: 而且我认为我们正试着少把它看作一个“这是好还是坏”的客观函数,

speaker: Unknown
en: And more of a problem of extracting and identifying people's tastes and preferences, which are not the same for everyone.
zh: 而更多地看作一个提取和识别人们的品味和偏好的问题,而这些对每个人来说并不相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a few pieces of this.
zh: 所以这里面有几个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is collecting the data.
zh: 其中之一是收集数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is also a nice potential advantage we have over some of these FAANG competitors.
zh: 我认为这也是我们相对于某些 FAANG 竞争对手的一个潜在优势,

speaker: Unknown
en: is that we have this large prosumer user base that we can actually learn from and use that to actually build a better enterprise experience as well.
zh: 就是我们有这样一个庞大的 prosumer 用户群,我们可以真正从中学习,并用它来打造更好的企业级体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's in the cloud, so we actually have visibility into what people are making, what they're doing, how they're prompting.
zh: 而且它在云端,所以我们实际上能看到人们在做什么、他们怎么用、他们怎么写提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're using that to sort of extract, taste, and see what works.
zh: 所以我们用它来提取品味,看看什么有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're running AP tests on different models to see what clicks.
zh: 我们在不同模型上运行 A/B 测试,看看什么能打动人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also able to combine different models from different providers in a way that some of our competitors structurally aren't.
zh: 我们还能够以某些竞争对手在结构上做不到的方式,组合来自不同供应商的不同模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're kind of tied into their own house models.
zh: 它们某种程度上被绑在自己的自家模型上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we get to directly test, you know, particularly in the world of image models.
zh: 所以我们可以直接测试,尤其是在图像模型领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all have a different feel to them and a different texture.
zh: 它们各有不同的感觉和不同的质地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we get to provide all of those for different use cases and see where they shine.
zh: 我们可以为不同的用例提供所有这些模型,看看它们在哪里大放异彩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us, it's not about the one right answer of evals, although we do have evals for a lot of common cases.
zh: 所以对我们来说,这不是评测的那个唯一正确答案,尽管我们在很多常见场景下确实有评测。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about actually using data to identify user preferences and eventually build models that tune to those.
zh: 关键是真正用数据来识别用户偏好,并最终构建针对这些偏好调校的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about short-term versus long-term opportunity, right?
zh: 你如何看待短期与长期的机会?

speaker: Unknown
en: One way to sort of think about that is that gap creates the space for the entire company.
zh: 一种思考方式是,这个差距为整个公司创造了空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other is that ideally you don't want to spend a tremendous amount of time solving problems that you think in 90 days or six months kind of will be completely solved with
zh: 另一种方式是,理想情况下你不想花大量时间解决那些你认为在 90 天或六个月内

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of some simple model integration.
zh: 就会被某种简单的模型集成完全解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's kind of this scaffolding approach where we constantly have to build out temporary supports and then take them away again.
zh: 有点这种脚手架式的做法:我们不得不不断搭建临时支撑,然后再把它们拆掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very strange approach to product building and we're even having to reorient our own mindset about how we build internally for that.
zh: 这是一种非常奇怪的产品构建方式,我们甚至不得不在内部重新调整自己的构建思维方式来适应它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The classic design mindset is make a quick prototype and throw it away.
zh: 经典的设计思维是做一个快速原型然后扔掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The classic engineering mindset is build durable systems that can last for 10 years.
zh: 经典的工程思维是构建可以持续 10 年的耐用系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: We find ourselves in this in-between where we have to build systems that last for six to 12 months.
zh: 我们发现自己处在这种中间地带:我们不得不构建只能持续 6 到 12 个月的系统,

speaker: Unknown
en: At a scale of 100 million people plus using them, but we also have to know that we're going to say goodbye to them and throw them away and build something new because model progress is so fast.
zh: 而且是在一亿以上用户使用的规模上,但同时我们也必须知道我们会跟这些系统告别、把它们扔掉、然后构建新的东西,因为模型进步太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you actually go about doing that?
zh: 那么你实际上是怎么做到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not going to claim that we've solved the answer to that, but I think a lot of it comes from
zh: 我不会声称我们已经找到了答案,但我认为很大程度上来自于

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineering things with the mindset of this will get thrown away later.
zh: 带着“这个东西以后会被扔掉”的心态来做工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it needs to scale by usage, but it doesn't need to scale by time, meaning that we don't need to plan for every future eventuality.
zh: 所以它需要按使用量扩展,但不需要按时间扩展,意思是我们不需要为每一个未来的可能性做规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: We often have to flag things and build such that they can be turned off again later.
zh: 我们经常不得不打上标记、这样构建以便它们以后可以被关闭。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say that's a core part of building.
zh: 我会说这是构建的核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like feature flagging as just an engineering technique.
zh: 比如说，功能开关本身作为一种工程技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it gets deeper culturally, and it's a cultural lesson that we're still trying to learn.
zh: 但我认为它在文化层面更深刻，而且这是我们都还在努力学习的文化课程。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also kind of jives with this whole move towards AI coding where, gosh, it's a shame we're going to throw this all away in six months, but at the same time we can build it four times faster.
zh: 它也和整个向 AI 编码的转变相契合，天哪，很遗憾我们会在六个月后把这些全都扔掉，但与此同时我们能以四倍的速度构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we should be willing to actually make more temporary things that we throw out later.
zh: 所以我们应该愿意实际去制造更多临时性的东西，之后再丢弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's like the inverse of this?
zh: 那么这件事的反面是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the things that you've decided have to be built for durability if a huge portion of what you build is going to be much more transitory?
zh: 如果你构建的东西里有很大一部分会更加短暂，那你决定哪些东西必须为耐久性而构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we have certain obligations to our customers, right?
zh: 嗯，我们对客户有一定的义务，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to keep their data private and secure, especially as we move into enterprise.
zh: 我们需要保证他们的数据私密和安全，尤其是当我们进入企业市场时。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have to keep serving these presentations, which are not always a one-shot episodic thing.
zh: 我们还必须持续服务这些演示文稿，它们并不总是一次性的、一时性的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're often these long-term living artifacts.
zh: 它们往往是这些长期存在的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have to serve them basically forever unchanged.
zh: 所以我们必须基本永远不变地服务它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't just go mess with someone's content after the fact.
zh: 我们不能事后就去乱动某人的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the things that are about how we store, render, and present things need to be extremely durable and sticky.
zh: 因此，那些关于我们如何存储、渲染和呈现内容的东西，需要极其耐久和稳固。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the mechanics of how we generate them, how we edit them, need to get thrown out even faster than we're throwing them out now.
zh: 但我们生成它们、编辑它们的机制，需要比现在更快地被丢弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's one more challenge with that, which is worth calling out, which is even as we move to AI doing more of the work, we are also in this world where users are trying to learn a complicated new tool to do a high-stakes part of their job.
zh: 但这方面还有一个值得指出的挑战，那就是即便我们转向让 AI 承担更多工作，我们也处在这样一个世界里：用户正在努力学习一个复杂的新工具，来做他们工作中高风险的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we can't just add 10 new buttons every month as new features come out.
zh: 所以我们不能每个月随着新功能推出就增加 10 个新按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still have to actually prune and simplify the user experience and maintain people's expectations of how things will work.
zh: 我们仍然必须真正去修剪和简化用户体验，并维持人们对事物运作方式的预期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so is most of that if there's no particular...
zh: 那么这些大部分是否……

speaker: Unknown
en: Way in which you've solved that other than it's a consideration and people have to use good judgment to sort of navigate it?
zh: 你解决这个问题的某种特定方式，除了它是一个需要考虑的因素、人们必须运用良好的判断力来应对它之外？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, but I think there's also maybe a design principle here which goes back to our prioritization which is err on the side of building fewer knobs and controls because all of those become things that you need to maintain and honor over time and they may end up becoming irrelevant as AI capabilities advance.
zh: 是的，但我觉得这里可能还有一个设计原则，它回到我们的优先级排序上，就是宁可少做旋钮和控件，因为所有这些都会变成你随着时间需要维护和兑现的东西，而且随着 AI 能力的进步，它们最终可能变得无关紧要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're now leaning towards this model of have...
zh: 所以我认为我们现在正倾向于这样的模式，即……

speaker: Unknown
en: Fewer, simpler building blocks, but then more open-ended customization on top, including even just like writing custom HTML, CSS, going with the grain of what models can already do.
zh: 更少、更简单的构建模块，但在此之上有更开放式的自定义，甚至包括直接编写自定义 HTML、CSS，顺着模型已经能做到的方向走。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the things that you've had to cobble together to get the product experience right sort of along this similar sort of path that we're going down that you're pretty sure will be solved in the future and thus you're sort of creating this sort of temporary solve?
zh: 在我们正沿着的这条类似路径上，你不得不拼凑哪些东西来把产品体验做对，而你相当确定这些问题将来会被解决，因此你算是在创造这种临时性的解决方案？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of what we've had to cobble together along the way have been guardrails that get an LLM to produce consistently good visual output.
zh: 我们一路走来不得不拼凑的很多东西，都是为了让 LLM 产出始终良好的视觉输出的护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to give some simple examples of that, if you are a company with an established brand, you always want to generate inconsistent fonts, colors, sizes.
zh: 举几个简单的例子，如果你是一家有既定品牌的公司，你总是不想生成不一致的字体、颜色、尺寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, even more basic considerations that matter to everyone.
zh: 此外，还有一些对所有人都重要的更基本的考虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: An AI should never write so much text that it overflows off the end of the slide and you can't read it anymore.
zh: AI 永远不应该写那么多文字，以至于溢出到幻灯片末尾之外、让人读不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Text probably shouldn't get too small.
zh: 文字大概也不应该变得太小。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on, the guardrails we took to that were hard structural constraints of our format.
zh: 早期，我们针对这个采取的护栏是我们格式的硬性结构约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, we didn't even let you customize the fonts on an individual block of text.
zh: 举例来说，我们甚至不让你自定义单个文本块的字体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of enforced them from the outside and said, LLM, you just write text and we will style it for you.
zh: 我们基本上从外部强制执行，并对 LLM 说，你只管写文字，我们会为你做样式处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same applies for layout, where we wouldn't actually have the AI
zh: 布局也一样，我们实际上不会让 AI

speaker: Unknown
en: Hard code XY positions of elements.
zh: 硬编码元素的 XY 坐标。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would have it give more semantic ideas like a three column layout and we would actually render that for the AI.
zh: 我们会让它给出更语义化的想法，比如三栏布局，然后我们会替 AI 实际渲染出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things have served us really well for both agents and humans.
zh: 这些东西对智能体和人类都一直服务得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even for humans, they remove a lot of the fussing that goes into making a presentation.
zh: 即使对人类来说，它们也去除了制作演示文稿时大量的琐碎 fussing。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of our core value proposition is taking away the fussy formatting so you can focus on content.
zh: 这差不多就是我们的核心价值主张：去掉繁琐的格式处理，让你能专注于内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: But frankly, we're finding now that it's actually hamstringing us by building all these guardrails in about formatting and design.
zh: 但坦白说，我们现在发现，围绕格式和设计构建所有这些护栏实际上在束缚我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're actually limiting what AI can do compared to just letting it loose with full creativity.
zh: 与放手让它 fully 发挥创造力相比，我们实际上在限制 AI 能做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of the hard problems we're digging into now is how do we actually give the AI more of a creative ceiling and in some cases kick away these guardrails that were previously holding it up while still maintaining that floor and the editing experience that is simple and focused.
zh: 所以我们现在深挖的很多难题是，我们如何真正给 AI 更高的创造力上限，并在某些情况下踢开这些之前一直托着它的护栏，同时仍然维持那个下限以及简单、专注的编辑体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: What has been your important learnings from a monetization standpoint?
zh: 从商业化的角度，你有哪些重要的经验教训？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think the biggest meta-learning has been that monetizing AI products is a moving target.
zh: 嗯，我认为最大的元学习是，AI 产品的商业化是一个移动的靶子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's no pricing model we could have had starting in 2023 up to now in 2026 that would have worked at every period of our growth or into the future.
zh: 从 2023 年开始到现在 2026 年，没有任何一种定价模型能在我们增长的每个阶段乃至未来都行之有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've actually had to have a monetization model that is adaptive with changing trends.
zh: 所以我们实际上必须拥有一个能随趋势变化而自适应的商业化模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to maybe call out a few of those key adaptations that we had to face early on.
zh: 举几个我们早期不得不应对的关键调整吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first discovery was actually a great one, which is AI products are easier to monetize than traditional SaaS products.
zh: 第一个发现其实是个很棒的发现，那就是 AI 产品比传统 SaaS 产品更容易商业化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The willingness to pay is just much higher, and there's a natural customer understanding that these things cost money to run.
zh: 付费意愿要高得多，而且客户天然理解这些东西运行是要花钱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's this natural equation people have of their own hours saved into dollars they pay for a software product.
zh: 人们心里有一个天然的等式：把自己省下的时间换算成他们为一个软件产品支付的美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we can save someone eight hours in a month and charge them $20, for many people it's a no-brainer and they'll happily do it.
zh: 所以当我们能为某人在一个月内省下八个小时并只收 20 美元时，对很多人来说这是不假思索的事，他们会很乐意这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're able to sort of compute that rationally, you found?
zh: 而他们能够比较理性地计算这个，你发现了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least they're willing to give it a try.
zh: 至少他们愿意试一试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're willing to say, yeah, 20 bucks.
zh: 我觉得他们愿意说，行，20 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think those numbers are usually far enough apart of what do I pay for eight hours of work versus $20 that many, many people are willing to just try it out.
zh: 我的意思是，这些数字之间通常差距足够大——为八小时的工作付多少钱对比 20 美元——所以很多很多人都愿意直接试一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there's a churn component on the other end of that, which is this AI tourism phenomenon.
zh: 但在这另一端还有一个流失的成分，也就是这种「AI 旅游」现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are very willing to try a new AI product, but just because they've swiped their credit card the first time doesn't mean they're actually committed.
zh: 人们非常愿意尝试一个新的 AI 产品，但他们第一次刷卡付费并不意味着他们真的 committed。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've had to learn how to almost filter within our revenue base and figure out who are those sticky users and how do we keep nurturing and growing them.
zh: 所以我们不得不学习如何在我们的收入基础内部做近乎筛选的工作，弄清楚谁是那些粘性用户，以及我们如何持续培育和增长他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you said, presentations are a naturally episodic use case, which means we can't expect on our prosumer base to have more than 100% net revenue retention.
zh: 正如你所说，演示文稿是一个天然阶段性的使用场景，这意味着我们不能期望我们的 prosumer 基础用户群有超过 100% 的净收入留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know we're gonna lose a lot of these people.
zh: 我们知道我们会失去很多这样的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to be okay with losing those people.
zh: 我们必须接受失去这些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be a mistake, though, to block them entirely from subscribing or, for example, limit ourselves to only annual plans and lose those monthly users.
zh: 不过，如果因此完全阻止他们订阅，或者比如把自己限制在只有年费计划而失去那些月费用户，那将是一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, because they're still a great revenue source, even if it's not always recurring.
zh: 首先，因为他们仍然是一个很好的收入来源，即使它并不总是持续性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second of all, because within that larger base, there are some who will really stick and see the value.
zh: 其次，因为在这个更大的基础用户群中，有一些人会真正留下来并看到价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And third, because there's still this viral loop that we kick off from these episodic users, who, by the way, do come back.
zh: 第三，因为我们仍然有从这个阶段性用户群体启动的病毒式传播循环，顺便说一句，这些人确实会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if it's episodic, it still recurs on a slower rate.
zh: 即使是阶段性的，它仍然会以更慢的频率循环发生。

speaker: Unknown
