en: And so for all those reasons, we want to keep nurturing this wide base of people who know and love Gamma and refer to their friends and use it sometimes.
zh: 出于所有这些原因，我们想持续培育这个广泛的用户基础——那些了解并喜爱 Gamma、向朋友推荐、偶尔使用的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also need to kind of look within that for the stickier user base.
zh: 但我们也需要在其中寻找更粘性的用户基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes there are different personas or ICPs within these.
zh: 而且有时候在这些用户里有不同的画像或 ICP。

speaker: Unknown
en: The type of user who will be the sticky recurring user using us every day of the week is not always the same as the person who's coming episodically, but there are more of those episodic people.
zh: 那种会成为粘性持续用户、每周每天都在使用我们的用户类型，并不总是和阶段性前来的用户是同一类人，但那些阶段性的人数量更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you just look at raw numbers, you can kind of get confused about where to focus your time.
zh: 所以如果你只看原始数字，你可能会对应该把时间聚焦在哪里感到困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how have you actually gone about this?
zh: 那么你们实际上是怎么做的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that map to the way you've chosen to monetize the product?
zh: 这如何映射到你们选择的产品变现方式上？

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of it is by monetizing our product through different tiers.
zh: 其中一部分是通过不同的层级来对我们的产品进行变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, pricing naturally reveals preference.
zh: 而且，你知道，定价自然会揭示偏好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, we have at the low end a $10 a month plan, which is relatively episodic.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们在低端有一个每月 10 美元的计划，它是相对阶段性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's our entry-level floor.
zh: 它是我们的入门级地板。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also more popular internationally in developing countries who don't have the money for very expensive AI products.
zh: 它在发展中国家也更受欢迎，那些地方的人没有钱购买非常昂贵的 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not actually a loss leader because we do make money off of it, but we never expect it to be the sticky, retentive product.
zh: 它实际上不是引流品（loss leader），因为我们确实从它上面赚钱，但我们从不期望它成为那个粘性的、有留存的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we have just kept discovering new ways to add more tiers of value on top of that.
zh: 但在那之后，我们不断发现新的方式来在上面增加更多层级的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a pro plan that's $25 a month on top of that, which is surprisingly popular even at a higher price point and naturally stickier.
zh: 所以我们有一个在此基础上每月 25 美元的 pro 计划，它在更高的价位上出奇地受欢迎，而且天然更粘性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's for, you know, bigger prosumers, people in more developed countries who have more money to spend.
zh: 它是给，你知道，更大的 prosumer、那些在更发达国家、有更多钱可花的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we've now added an ultra plan that's at the $100 a month price point.
zh: 然后我们现在又增加了一个 ultra 计划，定价在每月 100 美元的价位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's people who have much higher volume of usage, much higher expectations.
zh: 所以那是那些使用量大得多、期望值高得多的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're willing to use the fanciest AI models to get the best output.
zh: 他们愿意使用最高级的 AI 模型来获得最好的输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we can monetize them very differently.
zh: 这样我们就能用非常不同的方式对他们进行变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's also this new axis of individual versus team where we've built up team and business plans where we're now kind of spreading across the entire company.
zh: 然后还有个人对团队这个新维度，我们建立起了团队和企业计划，现在我们正在某种程度上扩展到整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the retention of those looks obviously much better than the individual plans.
zh: 而这些的留存率显然比个人计划好看得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the transition from a consumer prosumer company to one selling businesses feel very incremental or it feels just the gulf between those two things is very significant?
zh: 从一家消费级/prosumer 公司转型为一家向企业销售的公司，感觉是非常渐进的，还是感觉这两者之间的鸿沟非常巨大？

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted it to be incremental.
zh: 我希望它是渐进的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I thought we would tackle this was that we would inch our way upwards from individual to SMB to mid-market to enterprise to really big enterprise.
zh: 我原本设想的解决方式是，我们从个人一步步向上爬到 SMB，再到中型市场，再到企业，再到真正的大型企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: That felt like the kind of classic way to do it and also the sort of incremental sustainable way to learn as you go.
zh: 那感觉是经典的做法，也是那种渐进的、边做边学的可持续方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The pace of this AI industry has just upturned all of our plans in that respect for two reasons.
zh: 而 AI 行业的节奏恰恰在这一方面颠覆了我们所有的计划，有两个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is just competition.
zh: 其中之一就是竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't afford to leisurely work our way up the market because things move so quickly.
zh: 我们承担不起悠闲地沿着市场逐级向上走，因为一切变化太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then the second one is that the demand is just there.
zh: 但第二个原因是需求就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never would have thought that people in Fortune 25 companies want a product like Gamma right now because we started with these prosumer-y roots.
zh: 我从来没有想过《财富》25 强公司的人现在就想要像 Gamma 这样的产品，因为我们是带着这些 prosumer 底色起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, early on, maybe a year ago, they would come to us and I would just laugh and say, there's no way we can serve a company like this.
zh: 你知道，早期，大概一年前，他们会来找我们，而我只会笑着说，我们不可能服务这样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We shouldn't even have the conversation.
zh: 我们甚至不该进行这样的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what amazed us was even when we tried to turn away these customers, they kept coming back to us.
zh: 但令我们惊讶的是，即使我们试图拒绝这些客户，他们还是不断回到我们这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other way of arguing it is that the way a consumer uses a product is similar in that a business or a large enterprise is just a collection of individuals who are all trying to create material to talk to customers or clients or this or that.
zh: 另一种论证方式是,消费者使用产品的方式是相似的,因为一家企业或大型企业只是一群个体的集合,他们都在努力创作素材去和客户或顾客或这个那个交流。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did it seem like such a gulf?
zh: 为什么当时看起来像是一道巨大的鸿沟?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I'd been through a virtuous journey at my previous company, Optimizely, where we also started as an SMB product with $10, $20 a month plans, and over a period of, in Optimizely's case, several years, transitioned to an enterprise product with customers paying millions of dollars a year.
zh: 因为我在上一家公司 Optimizely 经历过一段良性历程,我们也是从每月 10 美元、20 美元套餐的 SMB 产品起步,经过(在 Optimizely 的案例中是)几年的时间,转型为一款企业级产品,客户每年支付数百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was very involved at every stage of that journey.
zh: 而我在那个历程的每个阶段都深度参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw what went well, but I also saw all the ways in which it was really hard.
zh: 我看到了哪些事情做得顺利,但我也看到了它在哪些方面真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to build up a sales team that can sell to enterprises.
zh: 建立一支能向企业销售的销售团队真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to market to those people and retool your motion.
zh: 向那些人做营销、重新调整你的动作真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to build a product that works for those.
zh: 打造一款对他们适用的产品真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out even when the individual user need is the same, teams have such different needs.
zh: 拐点出现在我们通过引入 AI 真正解决了产品内的病毒式传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's this whole world of compliance, privacy, you know, IT approvals and everything that you have to solve.
zh: 还有这一整个合规、隐私、你知道的、IT 审批之类你必须解决的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I saw how small our team was.
zh: 而且我看到了我们的团队有多小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we had maybe...
zh: 我记得我们大概有……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, 15 or 20 engineers at the time we started feeling this demand.
zh: 我不确定,在我们开始感受到这种需求的时候,大概 15 或 20 名工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not that we didn't want those kinds of customers.
zh: 所以并不是我们不想要那类客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just knowing the reality of what it would take to serve them was daunting.
zh: 只是知道服务他们所需的现实条件令人生畏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know how easily you can get pulled into these deals where you start making commitments to them.
zh: 而且我知道你有多容易被拉进这些交易里,开始向他们做出承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our philosophy was we didn't want to give up our prosumer products and only bet on enterprise.
zh: 我们的理念是,我们不想放弃我们的 prosumer 产品、只押注企业级。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to layer enterprise on top of this prosumer business that was already healthy, which meant that you have to divide your focus to some degree.
zh: 我们想把企业级叠加在这个本来就很健康的 prosumer 业务之上,这意味着你必须在某种程度上分散你的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have since grown the team a lot.
zh: 我们后来把团队扩大了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we've raised money.
zh: 显然,我们融了资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've probably more to triple the size of our engineering team.
zh: 我们可能把工程团队的规模扩大了两到三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've built up go-to-market.
zh: 我们建立了 go-to-market。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are now serving these companies.
zh: 我们现在正在服务这些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to answer your original question, it was not incremental.
zh: 但回到你最初的问题,这不是渐进式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a rapid sprint to actually be able to serve companies like that.
zh: 这是一场快速的冲刺,才真正做到了能够服务那样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Switching gears just a little bit, I think there's so many people that talk about we're in a time that distribution matters more than product.
zh: 稍微换个话题,我认为有很多人在说,我们正处于一个分发比产品更重要的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even in the early days when you had an inkling of this product, but it wasn't quite right, you had a lot of distribution.
zh: 甚至在早期,当你对这款产品有一点雏形、但它还不完全对的时候,你已经有很大的分发。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had a bunch of people trying the product.
zh: 你有一大堆人在试用产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you figured out about distribution?
zh: 关于分发,你搞明白了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I'll probably disagree with the premise here.
zh: 我想我可能会不同意这里的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: I still think product matters much more than distribution.
zh: 我仍然认为产品比分发重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is true, though, that increasingly, as AI products feed on their own training data, that distribution is how you make your product better.
zh: 不过,确实随着 AI 产品越来越以自身的训练数据为食,分发成了你让产品变好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think dynamics may change where people without distribution can't get their products to be good enough.
zh: 所以我认为格局可能会改变,没有分发的人无法让他们的产品好到足够程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I still think it's a mistake to conclude from that, that, oh, these are all distribution problems and we need to have a better brand and more marketing dollars and everything.
zh: 但我仍然认为,由此得出结论说「哦,这些都是分发问题,我们需要更好的品牌和更多的营销预算」是个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that absolutely matters, but I think ultimately product is the driver and great products can still overcome a distribution gap.
zh: 所有那些当然都重要,但我认为最终产品才是驱动力,伟大的产品仍然可以克服分发上的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: But isn't the early lesson of the story that the product wasn't right, but you also had tremendous distribution, thousands and thousands and thousands and thousands of people coming to the product?
zh: 但这个故事早期的教训难道不是,产品还不对,但你也拥有巨大的分发,成千上万又成千上万的人涌向这款产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I think that until we had nailed the product, we actually had pretty weak distribution.
zh: 不,我认为在我们把产品搞定之前,我们实际上分发相当弱。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had, you know, hundreds of people coming to the product every day, and every time we would do a big launch or a big marketing moment, that would spike to a thousand and fall right back down.
zh: 我们每天只有,你知道,几百人来到产品这里,每次我们做一次大发布或大营销时刻,就会飙升到一千然后立刻回落。

speaker: Unknown
en: The inflection point came when we truly solved virality in the product by introducing AI.
zh: 拐点出现在我们通过引入 AI 真正解决了产品中的病毒式传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point, we started getting distribution for free because people would make something great.
zh: 从那一刻起,我们开始免费获得分发,因为人们会做出很棒的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would share it with someone else.
zh: 他们会把它分享给别人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those people would try it out with a very low friction loop and tell their friends.
zh: 那些人会以一个非常低摩擦的循环试用它,然后告诉他们的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point, it didn't even matter how big that initial seed of distribution was.
zh: 到那时,最初那颗分发种子有多大甚至都不重要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What mattered was the slope of the curve.
zh: 重要的是曲线的斜率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that slope is all product.
zh: 而我认为那个斜率全是产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You spent most of your career building products before LLMs existed and CodeGen and everything that we have today.
zh: 你职业生涯的大部分时间都在打造产品,那是在 LLM、CodeGen 以及我们今天拥有的一切存在之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you're building a company that's completely predicated on this enabling technology.
zh: 而现在你在打造一家完全建立在这项赋能技术之上的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you describe the difference in what it means to be excellent at building products today versus at every other point in your career?
zh: 你会如何描述,在今天做到擅长打造产品,与你职业生涯中其他所有时点相比,有什么不同?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in many ways, LLMs have heightened what it always took to build great products and widened the gap between the teams that are really good at them and not.
zh: 我认为在很多方面,LLM 放大了打造伟大产品一直所需要的东西,并拉大了真正擅长的团队和不擅长的团队之间的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think actually the core trait that mattered before and still matters now is agility.
zh: 所以我认为,过去重要、现在仍然重要的核心特质,其实是敏捷性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by agility, I specifically mean being extremely close to customers about what they actually want.
zh: 而所谓敏捷,我特指的是对客户真正想要什么保持极其紧密的接触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shipping extremely quickly, faster than you're comfortable with, and then being willing to throw away or change your core product mechanisms based on what you learn.
zh: 以极快的速度发布产品,快到让你自己都不自在,然后愿意根据你学到的东西丢弃或改变你的核心产品机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: The kind of insane thing about LLMs is that agility used to mean that you would do all those things over, let's say, a six to 12 month cycle.
zh: 关于 LLM 的疯狂之处在于,敏捷过去意味着你要在比如说六到十二个月的周期里做所有这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's become possible, keyword being possible, to do them over a day to week cycle instead.
zh: 而现在,以一天到一周的周期做这些事已成为可能,关键词是「可能」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost no company can really stomach, though, the sort of g-forces involved in moving at that pace, and especially larger companies.
zh: 然而,几乎没有公司能真正承受以那种速度移动所涉及的过载力,尤其是大公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just too many stakeholders involved, too many legacy commitments and responsibilities that it's—I think it's just physically impossible to move at that kind of pace.
zh: 牵涉到的利益相关者太多了,遗留承诺和责任太多了,我认为以那种速度移动在物理上根本不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just impossible, but irresponsible to move at that pace.
zh: 不仅仅是不可能,以那种速度移动还是不负责任的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the bottleneck being humans.
zh: 而瓶颈在于人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only humans, I would say human decision-making is one, but also just the accumulated cruft of backwards compatibility, contracts, legal responsibilities.
zh: 不只是人类,我想说人类决策是一个,但还有向后兼容性的积累残余、合同、法律责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think even an org run by a thousand AI agents would actually hit this friction.
zh: 我认为即使是一个由一千个 AI 智能体运营的组织,实际上也会碰到这种摩擦。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that they're all a few months old, and so we haven't seen it yet.
zh: 只不过它们都才几个月大,所以我们还没看到而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're in this world where your ability to tighten that cycle time on all of those pieces is the key trait that will drive success.
zh: 所以我们处于这样一个世界:你缩短所有这些环节周期时间的能力,是驱动成功的关键特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: And companies in different profiles have to adapt in different ways.
zh: 而不同类型的公司必须以不同的方式去适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, for us as a roughly 100-person company, we already feel too slow.
zh: 你知道,对我们这样一个大约 100 人的公司来说,我们已经觉得自己太慢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We already feel like we have to be faster.
zh: 我们已经觉得我们必须更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see how a company of two or three people can just fly because they have none of this accumulated cruft.
zh: 我们看到一个两三人的公司可以飞起来,因为他们完全没有这些积累的残余。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can only imagine what it's like to operate a 100,000-person company in these conditions.
zh: 而我只能想象在这种条件下运营一个十万人的公司会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you figure out how fast you should actually be moving?
zh: 你如何确定自己实际应该移动多快?

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer's probably always faster at this point.
zh: 在现在这个时点,答案可能永远是更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think ultimately this goes back to diagnose with data, treat with design.
zh: 我认为归根结底这要回到「用数据诊断,用设计治疗」。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way to know if you're not moving fast enough is when you start seeing signals in the data that you're losing even an ounce of product market fit.
zh: 所以知道自己移动得不够快的方法,就是当你在数据中开始看到信号,表明你正在失去哪怕一丁点产品市场契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So looking at activity metrics, looking at segmentation of your users and how much they're driving your product, being kind of unflinching and listening to why people churn off your products and where they're going and what they're saying.
zh: 也就是看活跃度指标,看你的用户分层以及他们对推动你的产品起了多大作用,毫不退缩地倾听人们为什么流失离开你的产品、他们去了哪里、他们在说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to really sharpen all of those systems so that all of us are getting basically slapped in the face by data every day.
zh: 我们在努力真正打磨所有这些系统,让我们所有人基本上每天都被数据扇一记耳光。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we can use that as the ultimate signal that says, it's not about be fast or slow, it's be fast in the specific area.
zh: 然后我们可以把它作为终极信号,说明:问题不在于快还是慢,而是在特定领域快。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an area that needs drastic change.
zh: 这是一个需要剧烈改变的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an area that can make gradual incremental change.
zh: 这是一个可以渐进式改变的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an area that's crushing it and just keep going the way it was.
zh: 这是一个表现出色、照原来方式继续下去就好的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: You sort of gave the qualitative definition of your experience of product market fit while rolling up the hill versus down the hill.
zh: 你刚才给了你体验产品市场契合度的定性定义,就是上坡时与下坡时的对比。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had to turn that into quantitative metrics or numbers that actually express that qualitative feeling, what are the most important numbers that sort of express it?
zh: 如果你必须把它转化成定量指标或真正表达那种定性感受的数字,哪些是最能表达它的数字?

speaker: Unknown
en: The most obvious one to me in terms of like when I felt that things qualitatively changed was actually just new user signups per day.
zh: 对我来说,就我感觉事情在性质上发生变化而言,最明显的其实只是每天的新用户注册数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously a vanity metric, it's not the one that most drives the business, but it was the one that drove the qualitative feel of product market fit.
zh: 显然这是个虚荣指标,不是最能驱动业务的那个,但它是驱动产品市场契合度那种定性感觉的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to give some concrete numbers, before we launched our sort of AI product and it was more kind of esoteric and hard to use, we were in the hundreds of signups a day.
zh: 给一些具体数字,在我们推出那种 AI 产品之前,产品还比较晦涩难用的时候,我们每天有几百个注册。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as we launched this AI product, it jumped into the low thousands.
zh: 我们一推出这个 AI 产品,数字就跳到了几千。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're talking one or two thousand a day.
zh: 我们说的是一天一到两千。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the reason we knew product market fit was happening was that the numbers started inflecting upwards.
zh: 但我们知道产品市场契合度正在发生的原因,是数字开始向上拐。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it started inflecting to be very quickly in a matter of a month or two, 10,000 signups a day, 20,000, 30,000.
zh: 所以它开始向上拐,很快,在一两个月内达到每天一万注册、两万、三万。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is the opposite.
zh: 这正好相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: Normally you launch something and you go from a thousand to 600.
zh: 通常你发布一个东西,会从一千掉到六百。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the fact that it went up, I mean, it reminded me of reading about Facebook in the early days, you know, like a true viral coefficient was at work.
zh: 所以它上升这个事实,我是说,这让我想起读到的 Facebook 早期的情况,你知道,就像一个真正的病毒系数在起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were still doing no paid marketing at this time.
zh: 而且我们当时还没有做任何付费营销。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the only explanation for this was word of mouth growth, basically, you know, different kinds of word of mouth.
zh: 所以对此唯一的解释基本上就是口碑增长,你知道,各种不同形式的口碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that 10,000 kept climbing upwards, 10,000, 20,000, 30,000, to the point where in our first year we crossed 100,000 signups a day.
zh: 但那个一万持续攀升,一万、两万、三万,以至于在我们第一年就突破了每天十万注册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just tried to step back and visualize 100,000 people.
zh: 我只是试着退后一步,想象十万人是什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like a stadium.
zh: 那就像一座体育场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's really actually unreal this when people were signing up for this product that we hadn't even really marketed and still had major weak spots at the time.
zh: 我是说,人们注册这个我们甚至还没有真正营销过、当时还有重大弱点的产品,这真的太不真实了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was maybe three years ago.
zh: 那大概是三年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that number has continued to trend upward, not exponentially forever.
zh: 而且这个数字一直持续上升,虽然不是永远指数式上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd have the whole human population at some point if it had kept trending upwards.
zh: 如果它一直上升的话,总有一天会达到全人类人口。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it has settled in now, you know, well above 100,000 signups every day.
zh: 但它现在已经稳定下来了,你知道,远高于每天十万注册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that just keeps on going.
zh: 而且这还在持续不断。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of amazes me that there's this many people out there.
zh: 有这么多人在外面,这让我有点惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, now we think a lot more about signup quality and different markets and different job functions and all of that.
zh: 当然,现在我们对注册质量、不同市场、不同职能岗位等考虑得更多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was the clearest sign that we had gone through some kind of phase shift.
zh: 但那是最明确的信号,说明我们经历了某种相变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you then also think a lot about retention and usages as key PMF metrics or no, it's really...
zh: 那你们当时是否也把留存和使用量当作关键的 PMF 指标来考虑?还是说……

speaker: Unknown
en: The true definition of PMF is that you're so overwhelmed that you can't think of anything else.
zh: PMF 的真正定义是,你被压得喘不过气,根本无暇想别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we were for the first year, probably.
zh: 第一年我们大概就是那个状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't even think about are they using or retaining.
zh: 我们甚至无法去想他们有没有在使用、有没有留存。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just trying to keep all the people coming through the door.
zh: 我们只是在努力让涌进门的这些人都能被接住。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back to what we were talking about a second ago, what are some of the things you've had to unlearn or have been hard for you to unlearn in building products in this era versus the rest of your career?
zh: 回到我们刚才聊的话题,在当下这个时代做产品,比起你职业生涯的其他阶段,有哪些事情是你不得不忘掉的,或者是很难忘掉的?

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the hardest things is that we as a company value craftsmanship as one of our core values, building things really well and really carefully and really thoughtfully.
zh: 最难的事情之一是,我们作为一家公司,把工艺精神(craftsmanship)当作核心价值之一,把东西做得非常好、非常用心、非常深思熟虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think also part of that is we valued a culture of, I won't say consensus decision-making, but involving a lot of people, having a lot of opinions and letting those all shape the final output.
zh: 我想其中一部分也是我们珍视这样一种文化,我不说是共识决策,而是让很多人参与进来,听取很多意见,并让这些意见共同塑造最终的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of that care from our team is what drove our early success.
zh: 团队的这份用心很大程度上推动了我们早期的成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wouldn't say we've tried to unlearn it, but the pace at which the market is moving and the need to change the product has made us adapt that, our idea of what craft looks like.
zh: 所以我不会说我们试图忘掉它,但市场变化的速度和改变产品的需求,让我们不得不调整对工艺的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Craft can no longer look like going into your little studio and tinkering for several weeks before coming out with something to show for it.
zh: 工艺不能再是走进你的小工作室,捣鼓好几个星期才拿出点东西来展示。

speaker: Unknown
en: And craft also doesn't mean that all of us can feel the same ownership of the product through consensus.
zh: 工艺也不意味着我们所有人都能通过共识对产品拥有同样的所有权。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually have to take these blind leaps in the dark often.
zh: 我们实际上经常必须做出这些盲目的飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put something out there, see if it works.
zh: 把东西放出去,看看行不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have to sunset things a lot more quickly.
zh: 我们也必须更快速地下线一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think figuring out how to square high pace and urgency of innovation with craft and care has been one of the trickiest cultural adaptations to navigate along the way.
zh: 所以我想,如何把高节奏、创新的紧迫感与工艺和用心调和起来,是我们一路走来最棘手的文化调适之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even if it's not solved, what is the definition of craft in the context of your company today?
zh: 那么即便这个问题还没被彻底解决,在今天你们公司的语境里,工艺的定义是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it means that we still want to be our own best user of the product.
zh: 我认为它意味着我们仍然想成为自己产品最好的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still use our own love of the product as the ultimate North Star, but we have now tried to pair that with a much higher pace and a much higher level of urgency at getting things out there and much less sentimentality of keeping the things that we have in there.
zh: 我们仍然把对产品自身的热爱当作终极的北极星,但我们现在试着把它与更高的节奏、更强的把东西推出去的紧迫感相结合,并且对保留已有的东西少了更多感伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe you could say that it's pairing craft down to its essential, which is care without possessiveness.
zh: 所以也许可以说,这是把工艺精简到它的本质:用心,但不占有。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you zoom all the way out and you think about all the different things that you figured out about building an app layer AI company today, what are the most important things that you're reasonably sure are like globally correct?
zh: 当你把视角拉到最远,回想你今天在构建一家应用层 AI 公司这件事上想明白的所有不同东西,有哪些是你相当确定、几乎在全球范围内都正确的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: A few that come to mind is really obvious ones.
zh: 脑子里冒出来的几条,都是非常显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Multi-model orchestration.
zh: 多模型编排。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can't tie yourselves to a single model and just wrap that.
zh: 你不能把自己绑死在单一模型上,只是做个套壳。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to add value by orchestrating multiple pieces together.
zh: 你必须通过把多个部件编排在一起来增加价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: A simple example for us at Gamma is that we orchestrate both text and image models, but even in those categories we have probably three-ish major providers of each one and use different models for different tasks, in particular optimizing for cost, latency, and reliability.
zh: 以 Gamma 为例,一个简单的例子是我们同时编排文本和图像模型,但即便在这两个类别里,我们每类大概各有三个左右的主要供应商,针对不同任务使用不同模型,尤其围绕成本、延迟和可靠性做优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Building both evals on top and also a data pipeline to actually gather real user preference signals
zh: 在其上构建评测,同时也构建一条数据管道来真正收集真实的用户偏好信号,

speaker: Unknown
en: So that you can iterate on the quality, I would say is really essential.
zh: 这样你才能在质量上迭代,我认为这非常关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: On pricing, segmenting users into different types and finding ways to serve those different categories.
zh: 定价方面,把用户划分成不同类型,并找到服务这些不同类别的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how obvious this one is, but going international has been huge for us.
zh: 我不知道这一条有多显而易见,但走向国际化对我们来说是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The AI app layer opportunity is so much broader than just a narrow segment of people like say in the United States and the people right next to you.
zh: AI 应用层的机会,远比一小撮人比如在美国的人和你身边紧挨着的人要广阔得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think especially for a horizontal prosumer product like ours, it's just a no-brainer and our company is 10 times bigger than it would have been if we hadn't done that.
zh: 我想尤其对于像我们这样横向的 prosumer 产品,这简直是不用动脑的事,如果我们没这么做,公司会比现在小十倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if going horizontal versus vertical in general is a clear-cut answer.
zh: 我不确定横向 versus 纵向这个大方向上是否有明确的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope what we've shown is that horizontal can work, but certainly vertical can work too.
zh: 我希望我们已经证明的是横向可以走通,但纵向当然也可以走通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think it's important to pick, and it's very hard to waffle between those things, and you make pretty different choices if you do.
zh: 我确实认为做选择很重要,在两者之间摇摆是非常困难的,而且一旦选定,你会做出相当不同的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us as a horizontal company, betting on UX as differentiator has served us really well, and nurturing a team culture and talent around that has been really good.
zh: 对我们这家横向公司来说,押注 UX 作为差异化一直对我们很有用,围绕这一点培养团队文化和人才也非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about high-order bid insights, and you hit on many of these, around specifically building a modern prosumer business?
zh: 那么关于更宏观的洞见呢——你已经提到了不少——特别是围绕构建一个现代 prosumer 业务的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there kind of hard-earned insights that for other people that are just about to begin a prosumer business, you can kind of say, like, be careful of this, keep this in mind?
zh: 有没有一些来之不易的洞见,可以对那些即将开始 prosumer 业务的人说:小心这个,记住这个?

speaker: Unknown
en: Rethink pricing.
zh: 重新思考定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't take legacy SaaS pricing as a given in this new world.
zh: 在这个新世界里,不要把传统 SaaS 定价当成理所当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you'll need to test your way to pricing yourself.
zh: 我想你需要通过测试来摸索出自己的定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a live one.
zh: 而且这是条还在变化的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think our lessons will even carry forward in six months because the landscape is changing so quickly.
zh: 我不认为我们的经验六个月后还能适用,因为格局变化得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Differentiation remains really important.
zh: 差异化仍然非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you need a really crisp story of why someone should bet on you as a brand and you as a product because of an extremely concrete way in which you're different.
zh: 我认为你需要一个非常清晰的故事,说明为什么别人应该押注你这个品牌、你这个产品,基于你在一个极其具体的方面与众不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for us, if we're to boil it down into one word, it was speed.
zh: 我想对我们来说,如果把它归结成一个词,那就是速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should choose Gamma over PowerPoint because we are so much faster at getting you to the polished outcomes.
zh: 你应该选择 Gamma 而不是 PowerPoint,因为我们在帮你快速达成精致成品这件事上快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously we care about other things we've tried to layer things on, but we tried to really orient ourselves around that and then bring that into the onboarding.
zh: 显然我们在乎其他事情，我们也试图在此基础上叠加更多功能，但我们努力把公司围绕这一点来定位，然后把它带进新手引导里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's maybe the crucial one for a horizontal prosumer thing is you have to take your one value prop and show it in the first two minutes of when someone signs up.
zh: 这对于一个横向的 prosumer 产品来说也许是最关键的一点：你必须把你的那一个价值主张，在用户注册后的前两分钟内展示出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't do that, you're toast.
zh: 如果你做不到，你就完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And probably like the single biggest lesson that you could take from Gamma was
zh: 这大概就是你能从 Gamma 身上学到的最大的一条教训：

speaker: Unknown
en: Focusing on onboarding actually unlocked the real product's value prop.
zh: 专注于新手引导，实际上释放了产品真正的价值主张。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe to go back to your question of what we do differently, I would have just focused on onboarding.
zh: 所以回到你问的我们会做什么不一样的事——我会直接专注于新手引导。

speaker: Unknown
en: For my next company, I would say just nail onboarding over and over.
zh: 对于我的下一家公司，我会说：反复打磨新手引导，一次又一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you do nothing else, nail onboarding, because if you can nail the first five minutes, you've nailed the value prop of the rest of the product.
zh: 哪怕别的什么都不做，也要做好新手引导，因为如果你能做好前五分钟，你就等于抓住了产品其余部分的价值主张。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just to wrap up, something you didn't talk that much about is what was the emotional and sort of psychological journey of the company?
zh: 也许作为收尾，有个你没有太多谈到的话题：这家公司的情感和心理历程是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe if you go back sort of across your path to sort of PMF in the different chapters.
zh: 回顾你走向 PMF 的路径和不同的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it despair and anxiety?
zh: 是绝望和焦虑吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was always pretty light and people were just creative and trying things.
zh: 氛围一直挺轻松的，大家很有创造力，不断尝试各种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did it feel like as a founding team through the beginning of COVID all the way up until now you're having 100,000 people try the product on a daily basis?
zh: 从 COVID 初期一直到你们现在每天有 10 万人试用产品，作为创始团队，这一路感觉如何？ [[704→714]] 说来讽刺，我要说最快乐、最轻松的时光，恰恰是我们完全没有产品市场契合的时候，因为零 PMF 等于零责任、完全的创造自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ironically, I would say the happiest and easiest time was when we had zero product market fit because zero PMF equals no responsibilities, complete creative freedom.
zh: 讽刺的是,我想说最快乐、最轻松的时候是我们完全没有产品市场契合度的时候,因为零 PMF 等于没有责任,拥有完全的创作自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it didn't feel, it didn't feel anxiety producing that like we have nothing?
zh: 但那种「我们什么都没有」的感觉，没有让你产生焦虑吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Eventually it got very anxiety producing once that runway counter started ticking down, but...
zh: 后来当资金倒计时开始走起来，就变得非常让人焦虑了，不过……

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on, I would say our first year or two, we'd raise enough money that we weren't immediately worried about, like, will this hit?
zh: 早期，我要说头一两年，我们融到了足够多的钱，不会立刻担心这个能不能成。

speaker: Unknown
en: We knew we had some time, and so we were in an exploration period, and that was so fun.
zh: 我们知道还有一些时间，所以处于探索期，那段时光特别有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got the best sleep of my life during, I would say, those periods of the company.
zh: 我人生中睡得最好的时候，就是公司的那几个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then probably the worst period of all was the time when that clock started ticking down and I knew we didn't have PMF and the music was gonna stop.
zh: 然后最糟糕的时期，大概是那个时钟开始倒数、我知道我们还没有 PMF、音乐即将停止的那段时间。 [[704→721]] 那是我感受到的最大限度的恐惧、绝望和焦虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was maximum dread, despair, anxiety that I felt.
zh: 那是我感到最大的恐惧、绝望和焦虑的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once we hit product market fit, it wasn't all sunshine and roses.
zh: 但一旦我们达到了产品市场契合，也并非一片阳光玫瑰。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there was a whole new set of challenges.
zh: 随之而来的是一整套全新的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh, every day there's a new problem to be solved.
zh: 天哪，每天都有新问题要解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much to keep up with.
zh: 要跟上的事情太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this metaphor of pushing the rock up the hill and chasing the rock down the hill because I had to get illustrates that
zh: 我很喜欢这个把石头推上山、再追着石头下山的比喻，因为它说明了

speaker: Unknown
en: Neither activity is particularly fun.
zh: 这两件事都不怎么好玩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pushing the rock and chasing the rock.
zh: 推石头，追石头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the frustrating thing about startups is you don't get even a week at the very top to just sit and enjoy the view.
zh: 而创业令人沮丧的地方在于，你连一周的时间待在山顶坐下来欣赏风景都得不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: You immediately go into chasing mode.
zh: 你立刻就进入追赶模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I felt like we've been in chasing mode ever since.
zh: 我感觉我们从那以后就一直处于追赶模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not to say it isn't fun.
zh: 这不是说它不好玩。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many wonderful parts of the experience.
zh: 这段经历有很多美好的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't trade it.
zh: 我不会拿它去换任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's my dream.
zh: 这是我的梦想。

speaker: Unknown
en: But don't expect to ever get a break.
zh: 但别指望能喘口气。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't, if you're a founder, don't ever kid yourself of like, oh, there's just this one stretch, but after that it's going to be so much easier.
zh: 还有，如果你是创始人，千万别自欺欺人地想：哦，只要熬过这一段，之后就会轻松多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or this one exact or this...
zh: 或者这一件具体的事，或者这个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I hire this one exec, if I close this one candidate, if we get this one deal, it's all going to get easier.
zh: 只要我招到这位高管、只要我签下这个候选人、只要我们拿下这单交易，一切都会变容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It never gets easy.
zh: 它从来不会变容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then why is this of interest to you?
zh: 那么为什么这对你有吸引力呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You go from one version of pain to another version of pain.
zh: 你只是从一种痛苦切换到另一种痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you said, by definition, the entirety of the company will be this.
zh: 而且正如你所说，按定义，整个公司都会是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a recent new parent and I'm observing all the ways in which having a child is like having a company.
zh: 我最近刚成为新手父母，我发现养孩子和经营公司有太多相似之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my feeling about both in these last few years is that there is so much pain and just physical exhaustion, but also so much joy and pride that you feel along the way.
zh: 这几年我对两者的感受是：有太多的痛苦和体力上的疲惫，但一路上你也会感受到非常多的喜悦和自豪。

speaker: Unknown
en: This feeling that you have built something that didn't exist before and the joy of getting to create something magical with your colleagues every day is so high that it is worth the pain and challenges that you endure along the way.
zh: 那种「你建造了以前不存在的东西」的感觉，以及每天能和同事们一起创造神奇事物的喜悦，是如此强烈，以至于它值得你一路承受的痛苦和挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: In reflection, did you find sort of the lack of intensity and pressure and angst that existed in the early chapter of the company's life?
zh: 回顾起来，你觉得公司早期那种低强度、低压力、低焦虑的阶段——

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that a feature or because you had runway, it created too much space for too much tinkering and slowness or like, do you reflect on that at all?
zh: 那是优点吗？还是说因为你有充足的资金，反而为过度的折腾和迟缓创造了太多空间？你有反思过这一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do reflect on it, but I don't think it's a clear cut answer.
zh: 我确实反思过这个问题，但我觉得它没有一个清晰的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the one hand, I think the nature of a creative product that is so design oriented is that you can't build it in a pressure cooker.
zh: 一方面，我认为一个如此以设计为导向的创意产品的本质是，你没法在高压锅里把它造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: This goes back to this larger debate going on around 996 and whether everybody needs to be working 80 hour weeks and I think there are certain types of company that are well served by a 996 type culture because it's just a grind where there's very concrete legible work to do.
zh: 这要回到围绕 996 正在进行的更大的争论，以及是不是每个人都需要每周工作 80 小时。我认为有某些类型的公司确实很适合 996 式的文化，因为那纯粹是一种苦活，有非常具体、清晰可见的工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's way more work than people and whoever gets through it fastest kind of wins.
zh: 工作远比人多，谁能最快干完谁就赢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But creative products that are oriented around creating that special experience that are often about restraint and doing less, I don't think are very well served by this mindset.
zh: 但那些围绕打造那种特殊体验的创意产品，往往关乎克制、做更少的事，我觉得这种心态并不很适合它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're well served by creating space for exploring multiple different paths in parallel, dogfooding them yourself, coming to your own conviction with time.
zh: 它们适合的是留出空间去并行探索多条不同的路径，自己亲身体验（dogfooding），用时间形成自己的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been funny observing like the linear founder and the Corgi founder arguing about this on Twitter because they represent these two extremes of company really well.
zh: 而且看到 Linear 创始人和 Corgi 创始人在 Twitter 上争论这个问题挺有意思的，因为他们非常典型地代表了公司的这两个极端。

speaker: Unknown
en: We, I think, are more of those designing tool where we needed that space.
zh: 我们，我觉得，更属于那种设计工具，我们需要那种空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, I'm also cognizant that Gamma really only succeeded because of luck.
zh: 与此同时，我也清楚 Gamma 真正成功只是因为运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our original idea didn't work.
zh: 我们最初的想法并没有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: A world-changing trend came along just when we were at our load point.
zh: 一个改变世界的趋势恰好在我们处于负荷极点的时候出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, I mean, kudos to us for jumping on that trend.
zh: 当然，能跳上那个趋势，也得给我们点赞。

speaker: Unknown
en: But still, if the wind hadn't come at just the right time, our boat would have sank.
zh: 但如果风没有在恰好的时刻吹来，我们的船早就沉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do wonder if we'd had more urgency and speed if we would have gotten more maybe shots on goal.
zh: 而我确实在想，如果我们当时有更多的紧迫感和速度，是不是可能会有更多的射门机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the takeaway from that?
zh: 从中得到的心得是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The point that you just made?
zh: 你刚才说的那一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it that there is more luck in outlier companies?
zh: 是不是说离群成功的公司里有更多的运气？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 哦，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's a huge amount of luck in outlier companies.
zh: 我是说，离群成功的公司里有大量的运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no doubt about that based on my own experience and from talking to other founders as well.
zh: 基于我自己的经历，也基于和其他创始人的交流，我对此毫不怀疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only luck.
zh: 但不只是运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think that the boat metaphor is always valuable of if the wind doesn't come, you're going to sink.
zh: 我是说，我觉得船的比喻总是很有价值：如果风不来，你就会沉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, dealing with that wind and getting your sails in the right place and zigging and zagging at the right time takes a huge amount of skill and execution.
zh: 但与此同时，应对那阵风、把帆调到正确的位置、在对的时机左右转向，这需要大量的技巧和执行力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in terms of like, what does it mean for company building?
zh: 但至于说，这对构建公司意味着什么？ [[754→]] 我对这些想法的综合，也是我在 Gamma 努力应用的，就是你既要给自己留出空间去发挥创造力、去尝试很多想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: My synthesis of these ideas and the one I'm trying to apply at Gamma is you need to both give yourself room to be creative and try a lot of ideas.
zh: 我对这些想法的总结，也是我在 Gamma 试图应用的方法是，你既要给自己留出创造性发挥的空间，又要尝试很多想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you need to do it faster and you need to be extremely decisive and bold on when you have one, throwing the entire company's energy at it.
zh: 但你得做得更快，而且当你命中一个想法时，必须极其果断和大胆，把整个公司的能量都砸上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good place to end.
zh: 是个很好的收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for the time and the conversation.
zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间和进行这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really appreciate it.
zh: 我真的很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks.
zh: 谢谢。
